(2) There is no DELETE, no TTL, no cron, no retention job anywhere in E:/LDR/supabase — every call ever placed leaves a permanent row carrying a multi-KB SDP blob. (3) That permanent, ever-growing table has REPLICA IDENTITY FULL and sits in the realtime publication with zero subscribers, so every insert pays full-row WAL plus realtime fan-out for nothing. (4) The row is never marked cancelled/ended, so a stale invite stays answerable forever: tapping an old notification re-runs `handlePendingCall`, fetches the same offer, and rings a call that ended hours ago. (5) `net.http_post` is fire-and-forget inside the insert statement — no retry, no dead-letter, no way to observe that the ring failed; the caller is told nothing either, because `_insertInvite` is unawaited and its catch is empty. (6) The project ref is hardcoded in the trigger body, so the migration is not portable across environments.
modules.scale_reason: Unbounded growth of SDP blobs with full-row replication and a realtime publication nobody reads is pure cost per call. More seriously, the ring is a fire-and-forget pg_net POST with no retry and no observability, and a never-expired invite row makes stale calls answerable indefinitely.

modules.name: Push ring delivery (`reach-notify` edge function → FCM)
modules.purpose: Turns a `call_invites` insert into a high-priority FCM data message on the callee's device so a backgrounded or killed app can ring.
modules.tables: Reads `public.profiles` (id, fcm_token, display_name, couple_id) with the service-role client, bypassing RLS. Writes `profiles.fcm_token = null` on an UNREGISTERED/404 FCM response (:208).
modules.realtime_or_push: FCM HTTP v1 `projects/{id}/messages:send`, DATA-only (no `notification` block, deliberate so the app draws the disguised notification itself). android `{priority:'high', ttl:'30s'}` for calls (messages get 86400s). apns priority 10 + content-available 1.
modules.current_mechanism: Invoked by pg_net with no Authorization header, and the function itself performs no JWT/secret verification — so `verify_jwt` must be disabled for it, making it publicly invocable. Per invocation it builds a fresh RS256 service-account JWT (`crypto.subtle.importKey` + `sign`) and exchanges it at oauth2.googleapis.com for an access token — no token caching across invocations. Recipient for `kind:'call'` is the explicit `record.callee_id`; other kinds fall back to "the other member of couple_id". Data payload: `{type:'call', from_name, couple_id, call_id, video:'true'|'false'}`. Always returns HTTP 200, including on FCM failure, to avoid webhook retry storms.
modules.known_weaknesses: (1) No authentication: anyone can POST `{kind:'call', record:{couple_id, caller_id, callee_id, id, video}}` and cause a full-screen-intent ring on a target device, repeatedly. Recipient lookup uses service role, so no RLS stands in the way. (2) `ttl: '30s'` for calls means FCM DISCARDS the ring rather than queueing it if the device cannot be reached inside 30 seconds — a doze window or a brief offline stretch loses the call entirely with no trace. (3) Two extra Google round trips (JWT exchange + send) on every single push; the access token is valid 3600s and is thrown away each time. (4) `profiles.fcm_token` is a single scalar column — one device per user, by construction. A reinstall or a second phone silently steals the ring. (5) `display_name` is sent in cleartext as `from_name` and lands in a notification on a device whose whole product premise is a disguised launcher.
modules.scale_reason: An unauthenticated, internet-reachable endpoint that rings arbitrary users' phones is an abuse vector on day one of public scale, and it does two Google auth round trips per push. The single `fcm_token` column caps every user at one device.

modules.name: TURN / ICE acquisition (Cloudflare Realtime TURN)
modules.purpose: Obtains relay servers so two peers behind different NATs can actually connect; assembles the full ICE configuration for the peer connection.
modules.tables: `public.app_secrets` (keys `CF_TURN_KEY_ID`, `CF_TURN_API_TOKEN`), read with the service-role client. NOTE: there is no migration for `app_secrets` anywhere in E:/LDR/supabase/*.sql — it was created by hand per the function's own header comment. Client-side cache lives in SharedPreferences keys `turn_ice_servers` and `turn_ice_servers_at`.
modules.realtime_or_push: Neither — a `functions.invoke('turn-credentials')` HTTPS call with a 15s client timeout, made independently by each peer.
modules.current_mechanism: The edge function POSTs Cloudflare `rtc.live.cloudflare.com/v1/turn/keys/{keyId}/credentials/generate-ice-servers` with `{ttl: 86400}` and normalises Cloudflare's single-OBJECT `iceServers` into an array (the client accepts both shapes too). Client caching is three-layer: process-static `_cachedTurn`/`_turnFetchedAt` (fresh for 12h), a SharedPreferences copy rejected past 20h age, and a `_turnFailedAt` 60s failure backoff. `_inflightTurn` single-flights concurrent fetches. `_ensureRelay` gives the warm-up a hard 3s wall-clock budget before `createOffer` and then PROCEEDS WITHOUT A RELAY if it misses, clearing `_turnFailedAt` unconditionally first (:368). A response containing only STUN entries is explicitly treated as failure (`_isRelay` requires `turn:`/`turns:`). Final ICE config = 3 hardcoded STUN (stun.l.google.com:19302, stun1.l.google.com:19302, stun.cloudflare.com:3478) + whatever is in `_cachedTurn` + optional static `METERED_TURN_HOST/USERNAME/CREDENTIAL` read from the bundled `.env` via dotenv.
modules.known_weaknesses: (1) Every device mints its own 24h Cloudflare credential and writes it to plaintext SharedPreferences; a credential lifted off a device relays traffic for 24h from anywhere, and there is no per-call scoping, no revocation, and no server-side rate limit on minting. (2) Cache validity is judged entirely against the LOCAL device clock (`DateTime.now()` vs stored epoch ms, 12h/20h/60s windows) — a phone with a skewed clock either keeps dead credentials or discards good ones. (3) `_ensureRelay` deliberately clears the failure backoff on every user-initiated call, so a persistently broken function is re-hit on every press of Call. (4) When the 3s budget misses, the call proceeds relay-less and the ONLY signal to the user is a red banner reading 'calls only work when both of you are on the same wifi' — the app's honest description of its own fallback. (5) The static `METERED_TURN_*` override is read from a `.env` shipped in the APK. (6) The function does no caching itself: N devices × every 12h = N Cloudflare credential mints.
modules.scale_reason: Cloudflare TURN is billed on relayed bandwidth and there is no server-side quota, per-user cap, or per-call credential scoping — one leaked 24h credential is a metered relay for anyone. The fallback when acquisition misses its 3s budget is a same-network-only call, which is the dominant failure mode once users are on real carrier NATs.

modules.name: Peer connection, media and the call state machine
modules.purpose: Builds and runs the actual WebRTC session: capture, tracks, offer/answer, trickle ICE, renderers, mute/camera/speaker controls, teardown.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/call/call_controller.dart (`startCall` :442-484, `_ring` :511-522, `accept` :524-554, `decline`/`hangup` :556-564, `_openMedia` :632-660, `_createPc` :684-734, `_applyAnswer` :760-775, `_addIce`/`_flushPending` :777-795, `_teardown` :812-847, `_startConnectTimeout` :91-99, `_routeAudio`/`setSpeaker` :595-622); E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/chat/chat_screen.dart :551-559 (the only place a call is started)
modules.tables: None directly (see `call_invites` module). Session/partner data read from `sessionProvider`.
modules.realtime_or_push: All negotiation rides the `call:<coupleId>` broadcast. Media is direct SRTP peer-to-peer or via Cloudflare TURN relay — never through Supabase.
modules.current_mechanism: flutter_webrtc ^1.5.2, unified-plan. `getUserMedia({audio:true, video:{facingMode:'user', width:1280, height:720, frameRate:30}})`; voice calls pass `video:false`. Caller: open media → route audio → `_ensureRelay` (3s) → `_createPc` → `createOffer` → `setLocalDescription` → broadcast `offer` → unawaited `_insertInvite` → start foreground service → arm 35s timer. Callee: `_ring` is the SINGLE place that enters `ringing` (enforced by E:/LDR/mobile/test/unit/call_ring_invariants_test.dart) → `accept` opens media, `_ensureRelay`, `_createPc`, `setRemoteDescription(pendingOffer)`, flush buffered candidates, `createAnswer`, broadcast `answer`, enter `calling` (not connected), arm its own 35s timer. Trickle ICE both ways over the broadcast; the caller retains every local candidate in `_localCandidates` and RE-SENDS the whole list on receiving the answer (:766-774) because a cold-started callee missed the first trickle. Remote candidates arriving before `setRemoteDescription` buffer in `_pendingRemote`. `onConnectionState` is the only authority for `connected`, guarded by `identical(pc, _pc)` so a disposed connection cannot tear down its successor. Audio routing: video → `setSpeakerphoneOnButPreferBluetooth()`, voice → earpiece; `setSpeaker(false)` re-scans and is the only recovery path for a headset plugged in mid-call. Teardown disposes the stream and calls `_pc.dispose()` (not `close()`, so AudioSwitchManager actually stops), resets every flag, and bounces `ended → idle` after a 300ms `Future.delayed`.
modules.known_weaknesses: STATES: the enum is exactly `idle, calling, ringing, connected, ended` — there is NO busy, no declined, no reconnecting, no held. A decline and a hangup are the same wire message (`kind:'hangup'`), so the caller cannot tell rejection from a hang-up. An incoming offer while not idle is dropped silently (`if (state != CallState.idle) return`, :744) and the caller waits its full 35 seconds with no busy signal. `onIceConnectionState` only `debugPrint`s — an ICE `disconnected` mid-call is neither surfaced nor recovered; only `RTCPeerConnectionStateFailed/Closed` tears down. There is no ICE restart, no renegotiation, no bandwidth cap, no codec preference, no simulcast, no DTMF, no mid-call quality adaptation beyond libwebrtc's own. `_localCandidates` is unbounded and re-sent wholesale with no dedupe. The two `RTCVideoRenderer`s are created and initialised in `init()` and disposed only in `dispose()` — the provider is not autoDispose, so they hold native textures for the entire process. `_setAwake` holds a wakelock for the whole of `calling`/`ringing`/`connected`, including a 35s unanswered ring.
modules.scale_reason: The mechanics are sound peer-to-peer 1:1 and cost the backend nothing per call, but the state machine has no busy/decline/reconnect vocabulary and no mid-call recovery, so on real mobile networks a dropped ICE connection is an unexplained dead call. That is a quality-at-scale problem, not a capacity one.

modules.name: Foreground service and wakelock
modules.purpose: Keeps the process alive so call audio survives backgrounding and screen-off, and shows the ongoing 'On call' notification Android requires.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/call/call_foreground.dart (whole file); started at call_controller.dart :476 (caller) and :549 (callee), stopped in `_teardown` :816; E:/LDR/mobile/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml :201-203; `WakelockPlus.toggle` via `_setAwake` :854-869
modules.tables: None.
modules.realtime_or_push: Neither — a local Android foreground service (flutter_foreground_task ^9.2.2) plus `FlutterForegroundTask.initCommunicationPort()` in main.dart:82.
modules.current_mechanism: `FlutterForegroundTask.startService(serviceId: 512, serviceTypes: [ForegroundServiceTypes.microphone], notificationTitle: 'On call with $peerName', notificationText: 'Tap to return to the call', callback: callTaskCallback)` on channel `call_service`. The task handler `_CallTaskHandler` is EMPTY — `onStart`, `onRepeatEvent`, `onDestroy` all do nothing; WebRTC audio stays in the main isolate, so the service exists purely as a process-keepalive. Manifest declares the shared `com.pravera.flutter_foreground_task.service.ForegroundService` with `foregroundServiceType="location|microphone|camera"` and holds FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE / _CAMERA / _LOCATION. The wakelock is driven from `_setState`, on for calling/ringing/connected.
modules.known_weaknesses: (1) `start()` short-circuits on `if (await FlutterForegroundTask.isRunningService) return;` and the live-location sharing feature uses the SAME underlying service class — so if always-on location is running, a call's service start is a silent no-op and the ongoing notification keeps saying whatever location set. Conversely `_teardown` unconditionally calls `stop()`, which kills the location sharing service when a call ends. (2) `serviceTypes` is `[microphone]` even for video calls, despite the manifest and permissions being set up for camera — Android 14+ can refuse camera access from a service that did not declare the camera type. (3) The service starts AFTER the offer is broadcast, so the window between pressing Call and the service existing is unprotected. (4) `notificationTitle` embeds the partner's real display name on a device whose launcher is deliberately disguised. (5) Every failure is swallowed (`catch (_)`), so a refused service start is invisible.
modules.scale_reason: Not a backend-capacity issue, but the shared-service collision with live location is a per-user correctness bug that gets more likely as more users enable both features, and the microphone-only service type is an OEM/Android-version landmine on video calls.

modules.name: Incoming-call notification, full-screen intent, and the disguise cover gate
modules.purpose: Wakes a backgrounded or killed device, presents a ring the user can act on, and gets them past the disguise cover and app lock into the call screen.
modules.tables: None. Reads SharedPreferences key `fsi_can_use` (mirrored by `FsiPermission.refreshCache()`), and later `call_invites` via `handlePendingCall`.
modules.realtime_or_push: Push only. Data-only FCM message → `firebaseMessagingBackgroundHandler` in its own isolate → a local notification on channel `call_channel` ('Voice', Importance.max, vibration [0,800,600,800,600,800]).
modules.current_mechanism: The background isolate does `Firebase.initializeApp` → `FlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin.initialize` → `createNotificationChannel(buildCallChannel())` → reads `prefs.getBool('fsi_can_use') ?? false` → `showCallNotification(...)`. The notification is `category: call`, `ongoing: true`, `visibility: secret`, `fullScreenIntent: <cached flag>`, with title/body/icon taken from `currentNotificationStyle()` so it wears the device's active disguise. Payload is the pipe-delimited string `call|<callId>|<fromName>|<0|1>`. Tapping routes through `_onLocalTap` → `_routeFromPayload` → `pendingCall.value = CallTap(...)`; cold start also picks it up via `getNotificationAppLaunchDetails()` and `FirebaseMessaging.instance.getInitialMessage()`. Because a cold-started app shows the disguise cover and has NO router (and therefore no `/call` route and no AppShell), both `CoverGate` and `FakeNewsScreen` listen to `pendingCall` and run the entry gate with `forCall: true` — the hidden trigger is skipped but the biometric/PIN app lock is NOT, and the 1.2s intro splash is skipped so the caller isn't kept waiting. FSI availability is `NotificationManager.canUseFullScreenIntent()` on API≥34 (true below), queried over the `miles/fsi` MethodChannel and mirrored into SharedPreferences because the background isolate has no Activity.
modules.known_weaknesses: (1) THE NOTIFICATION IS NEVER CANCELLED. There is no `plugin.cancel(...)` call anywhere in the codebase (grep of the call and notification files finds only `Timer.cancel`). With `ongoing: true` it cannot be swiped away; it disappears only via autoCancel when tapped. A call that timed out, was hung up, or was declined leaves a permanent 'incoming call' notification, and tapping it later re-rings the stale `call_invites` row. (2) No accept/decline ACTIONS on the notification — the only affordance is 'tap to open the app', then get through biometrics, then find the Accept button. (3) It is a one-shot alert: no looping ringtone, no repeating vibration, no auto-expiry — the channel's single vibration pattern fires once. (4) `fsi_can_use` is a cached mirror; a device that has never run the foreground refresh, or whose permission changed since, silently degrades to a heads-up notification with no screen wake. The app also does not qualify for auto-granted FSI (it is not a registered calling app), so denial is the expected state on Android 14+. (5) The payload is a pipe-delimited string parsed positionally — a display name containing `|` corrupts the video flag.
modules.scale_reason: This is the only path that works when the callee is not already inside the unlocked app, and it is missing the two things a ring needs: cancellation and inline accept/decline. At scale the visible symptom is stale, undismissable 'incoming call' notifications accumulating on devices, plus a ring the user cannot answer without passing biometrics inside the caller's 35-second window.

modules.name: Killed-callee path, end to end
modules.purpose: Inventory of exactly what happens when the callee's app process is not running.
modules.entry_points: Chain: call_controller.dart `startCall` :442 → `_insertInvite` :103 → 20260628_care_call_push.sql `notify_call` :48 → reach-notify/index.ts → reach_notifications.dart `firebaseMessagingBackgroundHandler` :227 → fcm_service.dart `_routeFromPayload` :176 → cover_gate.dart `openForPendingCall` :59 → app_shell.dart `_onPendingCall` :160 → call_controller.dart `handlePendingCall` :120 → `accept` :524
modules.tables: `public.call_invites` (offer fetch), `public.profiles` (fcm_token, display_name).
modules.realtime_or_push: Push only on the way in; the ANSWER and all callee ICE go back out over the `call:<coupleId>` broadcast, which the callee subscribes to inside `handlePendingCall` via an UNAWAITED `reconnect()` (:123) — the answer can therefore be sent on a channel that has not finished joining, in which case realtime_client silently converts it to a REST POST.
modules.current_mechanism: Caller broadcasts the offer to nobody, inserts the durable invite, and arms a 35s timer. The trigger POSTs to reach-notify, which sends a high-priority data push with a 30-second TTL. The background isolate cold-boots Firebase, the local-notifications plugin and SharedPreferences, then posts the disguised full-screen notification. The user taps it; the app cold-starts behind the News cover, `pendingCall` fires, the cover runs the biometric gate (splash skipped), `showRealApp` flips true, the router builds and its redirect walks the whole onboarding funnel (requires `session.loading == false`, a profile, and a couple), AppShell mounts, its post-frame `_onReady` drains `pendingCall`, `handlePendingCall` SELECTs `call_invites` by id and calls `_ring`. Accept then opens media, fetches/uses TURN, builds the peer connection, applies the stored offer, and broadcasts the answer — at which point the caller re-sends its entire gathered candidate list because it knows the callee missed the first trickle.
modules.known_weaknesses: Everything on that chain is a single point of failure with no retry: no `fcm_token` (never registered, or nulled server-side by an UNREGISTERED response) → no ring at all; more than 30 seconds of doze/offline → FCM DISCARDS the push rather than queueing it; FSI denied or `fsi_can_use` stale → no screen wake; app lock enabled → a biometric prompt stands between the notification tap and the Accept button. The wall clock — FCM delivery + background isolate cold start + human reaction + app cold start + Supabase session restore + biometric + session load + a `call_invites` SELECT — is measured against the caller's fixed 35-second timer and routinely does not fit. When it does not: the caller broadcasts `hangup` into a channel the callee is not on, `call_invites` is not updated, the notification is never cancelled, and the callee is left with an ongoing 'incoming call' notification for a call that no longer exists — tapping it rings the same stored offer again, sends an answer into an empty channel, and burns its own 35 seconds. Separately, if the CallController already exists in-process (the user entered the app earlier this session) and received the realtime offer while the cover was up, `state` is already `ringing`, so `handlePendingCall`'s `state != CallState.idle` guard drops the push path — while AppShell's `ref.listen` transition detector never fires for a change that happened before it mounted, so no `/call` route is ever pushed.
modules.scale_reason: The primary real-world calling scenario — partner's phone in a pocket, app not running — depends on a 30-second-TTL push, a hand-mirrored FSI permission flag, a biometric unlock, and a full app cold start all completing inside a hardcoded 35-second caller timeout, with no cancellation, no retry, and no state reconciliation when any link fails.

modules.name: Call UI surfaces (screen, pill, stats overlay)
modules.purpose: Presents the ringing/calling/connected states, the in-call controls, the minimised return-to-call pill, and the hidden diagnostic readout.

modules.current_mechanism: AppShell holds `_lastCallState` and pushes `/call` on the inactive→active transition (idle/ended → ringing/calling/connected). `CallScreen` pops itself when state returns to `idle`, showing `takeLastError()` in a 5s SnackBar first (the one-shot error channel; `_readableCallError` maps permission/device errors to sentences). A red banner warns when `relayKnown == false` during calling/ringing.

(3) The `/call` push depends on `ref.listen` observing a transition — a state that changed before AppShell mounted (cold start, or return from the disguise cover) produces no navigation. (4) Every stats sample is `debugPrint`ed unconditionally, including in release-mode logcat. (5) The overlay and the NO-RELAY banner are the only diagnostics and they are on-device only — nothing is reported anywhere a developer could see it at scale.
modules.scale_reason: Client-side rendering only, no backend cost. The gap that matters at scale is observability: the stats exist but never leave the device, so field failures remain anecdotes.

modules.name: Key exchange + CryptoCore (the crypto under all of Closer)
modules.purpose: Give the Closer suite one couple-shared symmetric key so intimate text/photos are ciphertext in Postgres.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/mobile/lib/core/crypto_core.dart; E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/closer/closer_crypto.dart (ensureSharedKey, packMacAndCiphertext, packFull, byteaToBytes, bytesToBytea); E:/LDR/mobile/lib/core/supabase_repository.dart:137-186 (publishMyPublicKey / fetchPartnerPublicKey / keyWasReplaced); E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/closer/closer_screen.dart (_prepareKey); E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/settings/settings_screen.dart:328
modules.tables: public.partner_keys (user_id PK, public_key text, updated_at) — E:/LDR/supabase/partner_keys.sql. No other key state exists server-side. Private key lives ONLY in flutter_secure_storage under the fixed key 'miles_x25519_priv_v1'.
modules.realtime_or_push: None. Key publish/fetch is a plain PostgREST upsert + maybeSingle on demand. No realtime, no push, no invalidation signal — a partner's key rotation is only noticed the next time the other device calls ensureSharedKey.
modules.current_mechanism: Each device generates one X25519 keypair (package:cryptography), stores the seed base64 in flutter_secure_storage (AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true)), and upserts the public half into partner_keys. ensureSharedKey() publishes mine, reads the partner's row, refuses if it is missing or equals the string literal 'plaintext-v1' (CryptoCore.legacyPublicKey), then does ECDH + HKDF-SHA256(info='miles-closer-v1', empty salt) to a 32-byte key held in a STATIC field CryptoCore._sharedKey. AEAD is XChaCha20-Poly1305: 24-byte random nonce, 16-byte MAC. There is no ratchet, no per-message key, no key versioning, no escrow, no server-side key backup. Three different packing layouts coexist: closer_crypto.packMacAndCiphertext (mac||ct, vault + memory threads + afterglow gratitude), fantasy_jar_repository._pack and body_map_repository._pack (ct||mac — the OPPOSITE order, hand-rolled per repo), and packFull (nonce||mac||ct, afterglow photos). bytea is written as a Postgres hex literal ('\x…') string and read back by hand-parsing that hex. A row whose nonce AND mac are all zero is treated as legacy plaintext and returned verbatim on read — pre-2026-08 rows in every Closer table are still base64 cleartext in Postgres and still decode fine.
modules.known_weaknesses: 1) REINSTALL IS COUPLE-WIDE DATA LOSS, NOT DEVICE-LOCAL. android:allowBackup="false" (AndroidManifest.xml:54) means the private key is gone on reinstall/new phone. The reinstaller publishes a fresh public key; as soon as the OTHER partner next calls ensureSharedKey they re-derive a different shared key, and every Closer row ever written — vault, fantasy jar, body map, memory threads, afterglow — becomes permanently undecryptable FOR BOTH USERS. Only the device that rotated sets SupabaseRepository.keyWasReplaced, so the innocent partner is told 'N items couldn't be opened — your partner may need to open Closer' (closer_load_result.dart:39-42), which is false: it is never coming back. 2) No re-encryption/migration path, so this is unrecoverable by support. 3) The private key is stored under a single non-user-scoped key name, so two accounts on one device share one identity keypair. 4) CryptoCore.clearCache() has ZERO callers — the derived key survives sign-out in a static; SessionNotifier.signOut (session_provider.dart:244) clears neither it nor the stored private key nor the Memory-Threads PIN. 5) The whole shared-key model gives the partner the same key as you, so nothing in Closer is private FROM the partner even where the UI claims it is (see Fantasy Jar). 6) hmacTag() is documented as HMAC-SHA256 but is keyless 32-bit FNV-1a. 7) One in-memory key per process means everything after key derivation depends on the app being open.
modules.scale_reason: Phone replacement is a routine event; here it silently destroys the couple's entire encrypted history for both people with no recovery and a misleading error message. At thousands of users this is a continuous, unfixable support queue plus real data loss. Also blocks any server-side feature (search, moderation, retention enforcement, migration) forever.

modules.name: Closer entry gate / Modest Mode
modules.purpose: Hide the adult module until both partners opt in, and prepare the shared key before any sub-feature runs.
modules.tables: public.couples.modest_mode (default TRUE) — E:/LDR/supabase/intimacy_additions.sql. public.consent_state exists in E:/LDR/supabase/intimacy_tables.sql:8-18 but has NO client code at all (dead table). profiles.birth_date + profiles_must_be_adult CHECK is the 18+ gate.
modules.realtime_or_push: None. modest_mode is read from the session's cached couple row; the partner flipping it is not pushed. Key prep runs in didChangeDependencies on every screen entry.
modules.current_mechanism: CloserScreen reads session.couple.modestMode; if true it renders the 'A space for the two of you' teaser. If false it calls ensureSharedKey() and switches between loading / ready / waitingForPartner / error by STRING-MATCHING the exception message (closer_screen.dart:58-60: msg.contains("hasn't enabled") || msg.contains('partner')). setModestMode does a bare update on couples.modest_mode — either partner can flip it alone; the 'dual consent' is only an AlertDialog on one phone. Sub-routes (/app/closer/vault etc.) have no redirect guard, only unreachable-by-UI protection. SecureScreen sets Android FLAG_SECURE via MethodChannel('miles/secure_screen'), wired in MainActivity.kt:44-57 (real, not a stub); iOS is a no-op.
modules.known_weaknesses: Error classification by substring match is brittle — any future message containing 'partner' silently renders 'Waiting for your partner'. Dual consent is client-side only; the schema comment on modest_mode claims both must opt out but nothing enforces it. consent_state is a fully specified, RLS'd, realtime-published table that no code touches. No re-check on resume, so a partner disabling Closer does not close it on your phone.
modules.scale_reason: Consent for an adult module is enforced entirely in the client and by one dialog. At scale that is a policy/abuse problem (one partner enabling the adult surface for the other), not just a bug.

modules.name: Private Vault (Closer, couple-shared)
modules.purpose: Couple-shared encrypted notes and photos with retention choice and mutual-consent deletion.
modules.tables: public.vault_items (couple_id, kind, ciphertext bytea, nonce bytea, ad text, created_by, retention, reconfirm_due, delete_requested/-_by/-_at, deleted/-_by/-_at) — E:/LDR/supabase/intimacy_tables.sql:72-93. Indexes: vault_couple_idx, vault_reconfirm_idx.
modules.realtime_or_push: vault_items IS in the supabase_realtime publication with replica identity full (E:/LDR/supabase/closer_realtime.sql), but NO client code subscribes to it. In practice it is fetch-on-open only. No push notification for a new vault item.
modules.current_mechanism: Notes and photos are encrypted on-device with the couple key, AD = a per-item pseudo-random string from _generateAd() (built from DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch, NOT Random.secure) which is then stored in plaintext in the `ad` column. Blob is packed mac||ciphertext into `ciphertext`, nonce into `nonce`, both hex-literal encoded. fetchItems() does `.select()` (ALL columns, including every photo blob) for the whole couple, newest first, no pagination, no limit — every photo's full ciphertext is downloaded to build the list even though decryption is lazy. Photos come from ImagePicker with imageQuality:85 and NO maxWidth/maxHeight, so full-resolution JPEGs go into a bytea column, and PostgREST ships them as base64/hex (≈2x bytes on the wire). Delete is a two-phase flag: requestDelete sets delete_requested*, and VaultItem.fromJson computes 'expired' with DateTime.now().toUtc().difference(requestedAt).inDays >= 14 on the DEVICE clock. hardDelete only sets deleted=true.
modules.known_weaknesses: 1) No pagination and no column projection: opening the vault downloads every photo the couple ever saved. 2) retention='ephemeral' writes reconfirm_due = now+90d and NOTHING ever reads or purges it — there is no cron/pg_cron job for vault_items anywhere in E:/LDR/supabase (only breath_events.sql and reach_pulses.sql schedule cron). 'Ephemeral' is a label. 3) deleted=true rows are never hard-purged either; the comment says 'if a periodic hard-purge job runs' — none does. 4) The 14-day mutual-consent window is computed on the client clock; setting the phone forward 14 days makes canForceDelete true immediately. 5) vault_items.created_by / delete_requested_by / deleted_by reference profiles(id) with NO ON DELETE CASCADE (intimacy_tables.sql:79,84,87) — see the account-deletion note under Cross-cutting. 6) The AD is stored next to the ciphertext, so it authenticates nothing an attacker could not rewrite. 7) Row-level ownership is not enforced: RLS is couple-wide for select/update/delete, so either partner can flip `deleted` on the other's item directly via PostgREST.
modules.scale_reason: Unbounded bytea photo storage in Postgres with no purge job, no pagination, and a full-table fetch on screen open. Storage cost and query latency grow linearly with couple lifetime and blow up Postgres/PostgREST rather than object storage.

modules.name: Personal Vault + PIN (features/vault — a SECOND, unrelated vault)
modules.purpose: Owner-only notes and saved-media references behind a 4-digit server-verified PIN.
modules.tables: public.personal_vault_items (owner_id, type, content text, media_url text) and public.vault_pin (pin_hash bcrypt, failed_attempts, locked_until) — E:/LDR/supabase/private_vault.sql. RPCs set_vault_pin / verify_vault_pin / has_vault_pin (SECURITY DEFINER, search_path includes extensions for crypt/gen_salt).
modules.realtime_or_push: None.
modules.current_mechanism: Completely separate from the Closer vault and NOT encrypted at all. Notes go into personal_vault_items.content as plaintext. 'Saving' chat/touch media stores a URL or the string 'intimate:<storagePath>' in `content` and repurposes `media_url` as the display label; a fresh 1h signed URL is minted on open. PIN is bcrypt-hashed server side with a 5-try / 15-minute lockout; hardening_2026_08.sql:151 revokes SELECT on vault_pin.pin_hash.
modules.known_weaknesses: Two things named 'vault' with opposite security properties: the Closer one is E2EE, this one is server-readable plaintext, and both ship in the same app. Saved intimate media is only referenced, so deleting the underlying chat/touch object leaves a dead vault row. A 4-digit PIN with a server lockout is fine; the personal vault content itself has no encryption whatsoever.
modules.scale_reason: Plaintext personal content in Postgres is a breach-blast-radius and compliance problem at scale, and the naming collision guarantees a future engineer wires the wrong one.

modules.name: Fantasy Jar
modules.purpose: Each partner writes private fantasies; only overlapping TAGS are surfaced, never the text.
modules.tables: public.fantasy_jar_entries (couple_id, author, ciphertext bytea, nonce bytea, tag_hashes text[]) and public.fantasy_jar_reveals (DEAD — no client code) — E:/LDR/supabase/intimacy_tables.sql:38-57.
modules.realtime_or_push: In the realtime publication, but no client subscription. Fetch-on-open. No push.
modules.current_mechanism: Entry text is XChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted with the COUPLE-SHARED key, AD = the author's uid. Blob is packed ct||mac (note: reversed relative to the vault's mac||ct). Tags are mapped through CryptoCore.hmacTag() — which is a keyless 32-bit FNV-1a over the lowercased tag ('tag_<hex>') — and stored as a plaintext text[] column. The 'private' scoping is a client-side filter: fetchMyEntries does .eq('author', myId). Matching is done by pulling the partner's tag_hashes with fetchPartnerTagHashes and intersecting locally against a locally rebuilt tag→hash map.
modules.known_weaknesses: 1) TAG HASHES ARE NOT PRIVATE FROM THE SERVER. kFantasyTaxonomy is a fixed 12-item list (fantasy_jar_repository.dart:15-28) and hmacTag is keyless FNV-1a, so anyone with DB access computes the same 12 hashes in a second and reads exactly which kinks each user selected. The doc comment claiming 'HMAC-SHA256 hashed with the couple-shared key so the server never sees plaintext tags' is factually wrong about the code beneath it. 2) ENTRIES ARE NOT PRIVATE FROM THE PARTNER. Both partners hold the identical shared key and RLS is couple-wide, so a partner (or anyone with the APK and a JWT) can fetch .eq('author', partnerId) and decrypt with associatedData=partnerId. The 'shown only to its author' property exists solely in the Dart filter. 3) No pagination.
modules.scale_reason: The product's core privacy promise (soft matches, never the raw text) is enforced only client-side and the tag anonymisation is reversible with a 12-entry lookup table. That is a headline-grade disclosure across the whole user base, not a per-couple bug.

modules.name: Body Map
modules.purpose: Pin normalized points on a silhouette with an encrypted note attached.
modules.tables: public.body_map_pins (couple_id, author, x real, y real, note_cipher bytea, note_nonce bytea) — E:/LDR/supabase/intimacy_tables.sql:96-107.
modules.realtime_or_push: In the realtime publication with replica identity full, but the screen does not subscribe — fetch on open only.
modules.current_mechanism: Note text encrypted with the couple key, AD = author uid, packed ct||mac (its own private _pack, duplicated from Fantasy Jar). x and y are stored as PLAINTEXT reals with CHECK (between 0 and 1). fetchPins pulls every pin for the couple, decrypts each in a loop, and silently `continue`s on any failure (body_map_repository.dart:135 — this repo did NOT get the CloserLoadResult 'unreadable' treatment the vault/jar/threads got, so undecryptable pins vanish with no message). It also carries its own copy of ensureSharedKey rather than using closer_crypto.ensureSharedKey.
modules.known_weaknesses: Coordinates are the semantically sensitive part of a body map and they are cleartext — the server sees exactly where on the body each pin sits, only the caption is hidden. Silent row-dropping means a key rotation renders the map empty with no explanation. Third hand-rolled copy of the key-derivation preamble (crypto_core / closer_crypto / fantasy_jar / body_map all have variants).
modules.scale_reason: Cleartext body coordinates plus silent decryption failure. Volume is small, but it undercuts the E2EE claim and produces 'my data disappeared' reports after any key change.

modules.name: Memory Threads
modules.purpose: Encrypted milestone timeline (title/date/note/photo) with propose→accept→archive lifecycle, behind its own PIN.
modules.tables: public.memory_threads (couple_id, proposer, title_cipher/title_nonce, happened_on date, photo_cipher/photo_nonce, note_cipher/note_nonce, state, accepted_by, accepted_at, archived_at) and public.memory_revisits (memory_id PK, initiated_by, initiated_at, partner_acknowledged_at) — E:/LDR/supabase/intimacy_tables.sql:128-150, RLS for memory_revisits joins through memory_threads.
modules.realtime_or_push: Both tables are in the realtime publication; neither is subscribed by the client. 'Revisit together' is a DB row the partner only discovers by opening the thread — no realtime, no push.
modules.current_mechanism: Client generates a v4 UUID with Random.secure and uses it as AD before insert (title AD = id, note AD = '<id>_note', photo AD = '<id>_photo'), encrypts each field separately, packs mac||ciphertext, hex-encodes, inserts. happened_on is formatted from local date parts. fetchThreads does `.select()` — ALL columns including every photo_cipher — for every non-deleted row, ordered by happened_on desc, no pagination. State transitions (accept/archive/requestDeletion/cancelDeletion/hardDelete) are plain UPDATEs under couple-wide RLS. The PIN gate is MemoryPinGate: biometric via local_auth first, else a 4-digit PIN stored in flutter_secure_storage as 'fnv1a:<32-bit>' — the file's own comment admits it is not a KDF.
modules.known_weaknesses: 1) Full-resolution photos (imageQuality:85, no maxWidth) encrypted into a bytea column and re-fetched in full on every screen open. 2) The 4-digit 'hash' is 32-bit FNV-1a over a 10,000-value space — reversible instantly if the secure-storage value is ever read; the gate is device-local, so unlocking on your phone does nothing on the partner's. 3) Deletion 'mutual consent' is state='deletion_requested' with either side able to cancel, all client-driven; hardDelete just sets state='deleted' — the rows are never actually removed and no purge job exists. 4) memory_threads.accepted_by references profiles(id) with no ON DELETE CASCADE. 5) memory_revisits.upsert on a PK of memory_id means one revisit request per memory forever.
modules.scale_reason: Same unbounded-blob-in-Postgres pattern as the vault plus a full-table fetch, and a gate whose PIN storage would not survive scrutiny. Deleted memories are retained indefinitely, which is a data-subject-deletion problem once users are strangers.

modules.name: Afterglow
modules.purpose: Both partners write one gratitude (+ optional photo) after intimacy; on seal it joins a shared timeline.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/closer/afterglow/afterglow_screen.dart (screen AND repository in the same file, AfterglowRepository at line 451); afterglow_form_screen.dart (routes /app/closer/afterglow, .../new)
modules.tables: public.afterglow_entries (couple_id, happened_at, gratitude_a/nonce_a/photo_a, gratitude_b/nonce_b/photo_b, retention, sealed_at) — E:/LDR/supabase/intimacy_tables.sql:60-69.
modules.realtime_or_push: In the realtime publication; no client subscription. The partner is never told an entry is waiting for them — no realtime, no push, no badge.
modules.current_mechanism: Side assignment is by string comparison of the two UUIDs: myId.compareTo(partnerId) < 0 makes you 'A' (afterglow_screen.dart:594). Gratitude is encrypted with AD = the writer's own uid, packed mac||ciphertext into gratitude_a/b with the nonce in nonce_a/b; the optional photo uses packFull (nonce||mac||ct) into photo_a/b because there is no photo nonce column. Reads decrypt gratitude_a with the alphabetically-first uid as AD and gratitude_b with the second — which matches the write side. fetchEntries filters `.not('sealed_at','is',null)`.
modules.known_weaknesses: THE FEATURE IS BROKEN END TO END. startEntry() (the only write path the UI calls) inserts couple_id, happened_at, one side's columns and retention — it never sets sealed_at, despite the form's own docstring at afterglow_form_screen.dart:19-23 claiming 'The sealed_at column is set here'. afterglow_entries.sealed_at has no default and no trigger. fetchEntries requires sealed_at IS NOT NULL. So every entry a user seals is written and then immediately invisible; the list shows the empty state forever. completeAndSeal() and fetchPending() — the two methods that would set sealed_at — have ZERO callers (verified by grep across lib/). Separately: photos again go into bytea at full resolution; retention='ephemeral' is displayed as a label and never enforced by any job; fetchEntries does `.select()` with no pagination; a malformed row is swallowed by `catch (_)` with no unreadable counter (this repo also missed the CloserLoadResult treatment).
modules.scale_reason: Ships as a dead feature that silently discards user-authored intimate content — worse than absent. Everything else about it (blobs in Postgres, unenforced ephemerality) is the same scaling failure as the vault.

modules.name: Time Capsules
modules.purpose: Sealed collection of notes/photos/voice that unlocks on a date, on physical proximity, or both.
modules.tables: public.capsules (couple_id, title, unlock_mode enum, unlock_date, unlocked_at, created_by) and public.capsule_items (capsule_id, author_id, type enum, content_text, media_url) — E:/LDR/supabase/capsules.sql. Storage bucket 'capsule-media' (private) with folder-per-couple policies. RPCs capsule_seal_summary + unlock_capsule (SECURITY DEFINER).
modules.realtime_or_push: capsules is in the realtime publication and CapsuleRepository.subscribe() genuinely listens on channel 'capsules:<coupleId>' for postgres_changes so the unlock flips on both phones. capsule_items is NOT published. Proximity uses an ephemeral Supabase Realtime BROADCAST channel 'capsule_proximity:<coupleId>'.
modules.current_mechanism: NOT ENCRYPTED AT ALL — capsule_items.content_text is plaintext and media goes to the capsule-media bucket as plain objects with 1h signed URLs. 'Sealed' is purely RLS: capsule_items_select_unlocked only returns items whose parent capsule has unlocked_at set, and hardening_2026_08.sql:143 revokes UPDATE(unlocked_at) so the client cannot self-unseal. unlock_capsule() checks now() >= unlock_date for mode 'date' and 'both'. Proximity: each phone polls Geolocator.getCurrentPosition(LocationAccuracy.low) every 4 seconds and broadcasts {uid, lat, lon} on the broadcast channel; each device computes Haversine locally and calls it 'together' under 100 m.
modules.known_weaknesses: 1) PROXIMITY UNLOCK IS UNENFORCED. capsules.sql:91-95 only validates the date for modes 'date' and 'both'; for unlock_mode='proximity' unlock_capsule() falls straight through to the UPDATE. Any client can open a proximity capsule from anywhere by calling the RPC. 2) THE SEAL LEAKS THROUGH STORAGE. capsule_media_select (capsules.sql:116) grants SELECT on every object under the couple's folder with no reference to unlocked_at, so a partner can list and sign sealed photos/voice before the capsule opens. 3) RAW GPS ON A PUBLIC BROADCAST TOPIC. The channel is created with SupabaseService.client.channel(name) — no private:true anywhere in the codebase — so broadcast is not RLS-gated; anyone holding a JWT who knows or guesses the couple UUID can join 'capsule_proximity:<uuid>' and read both partners' live coordinates. hardening_2026_08.sql:24 itself notes couple UUIDs are not secret (they are the first path segment of never-expiring couple_media URLs). 4) Requires BOTH partners online, foregrounded, on this exact screen, with location permission and location services on, at the same moment. 5) Date unlock trusts server now() (good) but Capsule.dateConditionMet uses local DateTime.now() to decide whether to even offer the button.
modules.scale_reason: A server-side authorization gap (proximity unlock), a seal bypass through storage, and live GPS on an unauthenticated-by-topic broadcast channel. All three are exploitable by any registered stranger who learns a couple UUID.

modules.name: Intimacy Signals ('In the Mood')
modules.purpose: Double-blind mood signalling: you only see your partner's signal if you have an active one too.
modules.tables: public.intimacy_prefs (user_id, receiving_enabled, signaling_enabled) and public.intimacy_signals (couple_id, user_id, state text, window_expires_at) — E:/LDR/supabase/intimacy_signals.sql. Helper functions has_active_intimacy_signal() and my_intimacy_signaling_enabled() are SECURITY DEFINER to avoid RLS self-reference (42P17).
modules.realtime_or_push: Genuinely realtime: intimacy_signals has replica identity full, is in supabase_realtime, and IntimacyRepository.subscribe() listens on 'intimacy:<coupleId>' for all postgres_changes filtered by couple_id. The channel lives on an autoDispose StateNotifier, so it exists only while the screen is mounted. NO push notification — a signal sent while the partner is backgrounded is never surfaced; they must open the screen inside the 6-hour window.
modules.current_mechanism: NOT ENCRYPTED — `state` is one of five plaintext keys ('thinking_of_you', 'feeling_close', 'missing_touch', 'feeling_flirty', 'wish_here') in a text column. sendSignal() deletes your prior rows then inserts one with window_expires_at = client DateTime.now().toUtc() + 6h. The double-blind property is real and server-enforced: intimacy_signals_select requires user_id = auth.uid() OR has_active_intimacy_signal(), evaluated against server now(). Insert additionally requires my_intimacy_signaling_enabled(). 'Not tonight' is a hard DELETE of your rows.
modules.known_weaknesses: 1) window_expires_at is chosen by the client — a modified client can write a 10-year window and permanently satisfy has_active_intimacy_signal(), i.e. permanently see the partner's signals without meaningfully signalling. IntimacySignal.isActive also compares against the local clock. 2) receiving_enabled is never enforced anywhere server-side (only signaling_enabled is) — it is a client-side display flag. 3) No expiry job: rows sit forever past window_expires_at, only filtered by query predicates. 4) Delivery depends on the partner having the screen open; there is no push path in reach-notify or any SQL trigger for this table. 5) The RLS select policy is evaluated per row against a SECURITY DEFINER function — an EXISTS subquery per row per delivery, on a table with an index on (couple_id, window_expires_at) but not on user_id.
modules.scale_reason: The consent property that defines the feature is bypassable by a client-controlled expiry, and delivery silently depends on the partner being in the app. Unbounded row growth with no purge.

modules.name: Touch Map (the shipped one — broadcast only)
modules.purpose: Live touch/reaction overlay on the partner's body photo or a silhouette.
modules.tables: NONE for the touches. public.body_touches EXISTS (E:/LDR/supabase/body_touches.sql, RLS'd, replica identity full, in the realtime publication) but TouchMapRepository.sendTouch() and TouchMapRepository.subscribe() have ZERO callers — verified by grep across lib/. The table is dead. What IS used: public.presence.body_photo_path plus the 'couple_intimate' storage bucket, and the RPC clear_body_photo (E:/LDR/supabase/touch_photo_delete.sql).
modules.realtime_or_push: Pure ephemeral broadcast on channel 'touch:<coupleId>' with five events: touch, frame, photo, neon, reaction_gif, wrapped in ManagedSubscription so it re-arms on socket resume. Nothing is persisted; nothing is pushed. Both phones must be on this screen simultaneously or the touch is simply lost.
modules.current_mechanism: Touch coordinates, neon trails and reaction placements are JSON broadcast payloads. Body photos are uploaded to couple_intimate at '<coupleId>/body/<uid>_<ms>.jpg' and rendered via a 1-hour signed URL fetched on screen open. Reaction GIFs/photos are uploaded to '<coupleId>/reactions/<uuid>.<ext>', a 1-hour SIGNED URL is minted, and that URL is put on the broadcast payload for the partner to load; the reaction auto-fades after 8 s client-side. Haptics are driven locally by a gesture classifier. FLAG_SECURE is set for the screen.
modules.known_weaknesses: 1) SIGNED URLs FOR INTIMATE MEDIA TRAVEL OVER A NON-PRIVATE BROADCAST TOPIC. No channel in the codebase is created with private:true, so 'touch:<coupleUuid>' is joinable by any authenticated user who knows the couple UUID, who then receives working 1-hour signed URLs to intimate photos. 2) Uploaded reaction objects are never deleted — only chat media and body photos have cleanup paths (chat_media_cleanup.sql, clear_body_photo); '<coupleId>/reactions/*' accumulates in couple_intimate forever. 3) The couple_intimate bucket itself is NOT created or policy-defined in ANY file under E:/LDR/supabase — its RLS lives only in the dashboard, unversioned and unreviewable. 4) body_touches is a fully built, RLS'd, realtime-published dead table whose expires_at default (now()+10s) has no purge job. 5) Nothing here is encrypted.
modules.scale_reason: Intimate-media signed URLs broadcast on a topic keyed by a non-secret UUID, on a bucket whose policies are not in source control, with unbounded storage growth and no retention. This is the highest-consequence disclosure surface in the suite.

modules.name: Touch Trace
modules.purpose: Two-way live finger-drawing canvas.
modules.tables: None. Nothing is persisted.
modules.realtime_or_push: Ephemeral broadcast on 'touch_trace:<coupleId>' with events stroke_point, stroke_end, clear. Strokes are throttled to ~30 fps (33 ms). Re-subscribes on realtimeResumed. No push.
modules.current_mechanism: Each pan update normalizes to 0..1 against the canvas constraints and broadcasts {from, stroke, point}. The receiver appends to a local stroke list, deciding whether a point starts a new incoming stroke by comparing the last stroke's ARGB against its own current colour (touch_trace_canvas.dart:105-110). FLAG_SECURE is set. Not encrypted (payloads are plain JSON over the realtime socket).
modules.known_weaknesses: 1) Requires both partners online, foregrounded, and on this exact screen — otherwise the drawing goes nowhere. 2) The incoming-stroke heuristic is colour equality: if the partner picks the same colour from the shared 6-colour palette, their strokes merge into yours. 3) It uses raw channel()/unsubscribe() + a manual realtimeResumed listener instead of ManagedSubscription — exactly the duplicate-topic 'joined but dead channel' pattern that realtime_service.dart:76-95 documents as the app-wide bug this primitive was written to fix. 4) ~30 messages/second/user on a shared broadcast topic with no backpressure. 5) Non-private topic, same guessable-couple-UUID exposure as Touch Map.
modules.scale_reason: 30 msg/s per active session is the heaviest realtime consumer in the app and it uses the known-buggy subscription pattern, so reconnect storms leave dead channels. No data at risk beyond the drawing itself.

modules.name: Mood Lamp
modules.purpose: Pick a colour; it glows on the partner's screen.
modules.tables: public.mood_lamp EXISTS (couple_id, user_id, color_rgb, updated_at — intimacy_tables.sql:30-36), is RLS'd and in the realtime publication, and is NEVER read or written by any client code. Dead table.
modules.realtime_or_push: Ephemeral broadcast on 'mood_lamp:<coupleId>', event 'mood', via ManagedSubscription. No persistence, no push.
modules.current_mechanism: Sends {from, rgb} on colour pick. A local Timer fades the lamp back to 'off' after 4 hours by re-broadcasting the dark swatch. If the partner is not on the screen at that instant, the colour is lost; on next open the lamp reads dark regardless of what was 'set'.
modules.known_weaknesses: State is a lie: the feature presents as persistent ambient state but is fire-and-forget broadcast, so it only works while both people are simultaneously on the screen. The 4-hour auto-fade Timer dies with the widget. The schema author clearly intended mood_lamp to be the store — it is orphaned.
modules.scale_reason: Low traffic and no data at risk; the cost is a permanently broken-feeling feature and a dead table carrying realtime replication overhead.

modules.name: Desire Temperature
modules.purpose: Both rate desire 1-10 daily; the partner's number is revealed only if both are >= 7.
modules.tables: public.desire_temps (couple_id, on_date date, user_id, score int CHECK 1..10, PK(couple_id,on_date,user_id)) — intimacy_tables.sql:21-27.
modules.realtime_or_push: Real postgres_changes subscription on 'desire_temps:<coupleId>' via ManagedSubscription, so the reveal re-checks when the partner submits. No push.
modules.current_mechanism: NOT ENCRYPTED — score is a plain int. Both submit and load compute the date string from the DEVICE clock: DateTime.now().toUtc() formatted as YYYY-MM-DD (desire_temp_screen.dart:68-70 and 110-112). The query selects user_id and score for the whole couple on that date, then the REVEAL GATE IS APPLIED IN DART: `if (mine != null && partner != null && mine >= 7 && partner >= 7)`.
modules.known_weaknesses: 1) The reveal gate is client-side only. RLS (desire_temps_select_member) returns the partner's score to the wire unconditionally, so the partner's number is in the HTTP response even when the UI hides it — trivially read with any proxy or a patched APK. 2) The 'day' is the device's UTC date: partners in different timezones, or a phone with a skewed clock, land on different on_date keys and never match. 3) Scores are plaintext in Postgres with no retention limit.
modules.scale_reason: The single privacy rule of the feature is not enforced server-side, and the day-key comes from the client clock — which breaks for exactly the long-distance, cross-timezone couples the app is for.

modules.name: Pick for us (dice)
modules.purpose: Roll a random suggestion tag per consented tier.
modules.tables: public.dice_rolls (couple_id, rolled_at, tier, result_tags text[]) and public.dice_tier_consents (couple_id, tier, user_id, granted, granted_at) — intimacy_tables.sql:110-125.
modules.realtime_or_push: Both are in the realtime publication; no client subscription. Fetch on open.
modules.current_mechanism: NOT ENCRYPTED. Tiers and their tag pools are compile-time constants in the DiceTier enum. Rolls use dart:math Random (not secure, fine here). saveRoll inserts the tier and chosen tags in plaintext. Consent is an upsert per (couple, tier, user); setMyConsent re-reads all consents afterwards and returns both partners' booleans so the caller can tell if a tier just unlocked — the unlock decision itself is client-side.
modules.known_weaknesses: Tier consent is enforced only in Dart; RLS lets either partner insert a dice_rolls row for any tier regardless of dice_tier_consents. Roll history (which explicit tier a couple enabled and what came up) is plaintext and retained forever. No pagination beyond the hardcoded limit 12.
modules.scale_reason: Small data volume; the exposure is plaintext preference history rather than availability or cost. Consent-bypass is only partner-to-partner.

modules.name: Home dashboard
modules.purpose: Landing tab: partner's status (online, mood, their local time, current screen), check-in snap, location card, cycle card, Reach button, half-paired invite-code recovery.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/home/home_screen.dart (tab 0 of E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/shell/app_shell.dart); check-in camera via context.push('/app/rapid-camera', extra:{'mode':'checkin'}) → E:/LDR/mobile/lib/core/router.dart:160-169
modules.tables: presence (read partner row, write own), profiles, couples, pairing_invites (activePairingInvite / create_pairing_invite RPC), storage bucket couple_media (checkins/<uid>_<ms>.jpg, PUBLIC bucket, getPublicUrl at home_screen.dart:130)
modules.realtime_or_push: partnerPresenceProvider: postgres_changes on `presence` filtered by couple_id, PLUS an unconditional 15s Timer.periodic full-row refetch (presence_service.dart:436) PLUS an 800ms debounce refetch on every event. No push.
modules.current_mechanism: While Home is mounted AND foregrounded, _startLocationUpdates() runs a 15s Timer that calls LocationService.shareCurrent(coupleId) — which does a SELECT on presence (fetchMine) to re-read the saved mode, then a device GPS read, then (mode!='off') a reverse-geocode via the OS Geocoder, then an UPSERT on presence. Home also calls Geolocator.getLastKnownPosition() every 15s for its own distance readout. Online-ness is not the DB is_online flag: Presence.isTrulyOnline compares app_last_active_at (stamped server-side by a BEFORE trigger, presence_server_time.sql) against ServerClock.now() with a 45s window, fed by a 30s foreground heartbeat in main.dart:203. Check-in: rapid camera returns a baked File, Home uploads it to couple_media and writes the public URL to presence.checkin_photo_url.
modules.known_weaknesses: Location sharing is foreground-and-Home-only: leaving the Home tab (not even the app) cancels the timer, so the partner's map silently freezes while the app is still open on Chat. Two DB round-trips + one geocode per user per 15s just to publish a position. didChangeAppLifecycleState cancels on any non-resumed state but only restarts from Home's resume. The public couple_media check-in URL never expires and the couple_id is the first path segment (documented as an attack surface in hardening_2026_08.sql:25).
modules.scale_reason: Per active user with Home open: 4 presence SELECTs + 4 presence UPSERTs + 4 geocodes per minute for location, plus 4 presence SELECTs/min from the provider poll, plus 2 heartbeat upserts/min. That is ~14 DB ops/user/minute at idle before anyone touches anything; 1,000 concurrent users ≈ 14k writes+reads/min against one Postgres row set with replica identity full and realtime fan-out on every write.

modules.name: Partner location card / 2D map / 3D map
modules.purpose: Show the partner's live position, distance, 'updated Xs ago', and a full-screen 3D satellite view.
modules.tables: presence.latitude/longitude/location_accuracy/location_label/location_sharing_mode/location_updated_at
modules.realtime_or_push: Consumes partnerPresenceProvider only (postgres_changes + 15s poll). location_map_screen adds its own 15s Timer for the user's OWN last-known position.
modules.current_mechanism: flutter_map with raster tiles from https://tile.basemaps.cartocdn.com/rastertiles/voyager (partner_location_card.dart:236, location_map_screen.dart:200) — CARTO's free public basemap CDN, no API key, no account. Map3DScreen builds an HTML string and loads it into a WebView with JavaScriptMode.unrestricted; that page pulls MapLibre GL JS from https://unpkg.com/maplibre-gl@4.7.1 and tiles from ArcGIS World_Imagery, s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod and tiles.openfreemap.org (map_3d_screen.dart:77-98).
modules.known_weaknesses: Four unpaid third-party endpoints with no key, no contract, and no fallback; CARTO and openfreemap both rate-limit and their ToS forbid heavy commercial use. The 3D map executes remote JavaScript fetched at runtime inside an unrestricted WebView — a supply-chain injection path straight into an app whose whole premise is hiding. Precise coordinates are stored in plaintext in the presence table (not encrypted, unlike the Closer module).
modules.scale_reason: Free tile CDNs will throttle or block the app's User-Agent long before thousands of users; the map is on the HOME screen, so every session hits it. Requires migrating to a paid tile provider (or self-hosting) before launch.

modules.name: Care reminders (nudges)
modules.purpose: Send the partner a preset or custom 'take care' nudge; the recipient taps Done and the sender sees the acknowledgement.
modules.tables: care_nudges (couple_id, from_user, kind, message, created_at, acknowledged_at) — THIS TABLE HAS NO DDL ANYWHERE IN E:/LDR/supabase. Only a trigger references it (20260628_care_call_push.sql:39-42). Its columns, indexes and RLS policies exist only in the live database.
modules.realtime_or_push: postgres_changes on care_nudges filtered by couple_id (care_repository.dart:71-88) wrapped in ManagedSubscription; plus FCM: an AFTER INSERT trigger calls notify_care() → pg_net POST → reach-notify edge function → data-only FCM message type='care' → firebaseMessagingBackgroundHandler shows a generic 'Reminders' notification.
modules.current_mechanism: Plain INSERT of a plaintext message row; acknowledge() is a client-side UPDATE stamping acknowledged_at with the DEVICE clock (care_repository.dart:57). The screen refetches the last 50 rows on every realtime event (no incremental apply). Send errors are swallowed by an empty catch (care_screen.dart:93) so a failed insert produces no toast and no error — it just silently does nothing.
modules.known_weaknesses: The push notification carries no text at all (disguise requirement, reach_notifications.dart:199-223) — the whole nudge is 'Take your medicine' and the recipient sees a blank generic alert, so the feature does not deliver what it promises unless the app is opened. Any couple member can UPDATE acknowledged_at on a nudge they sent (RLS unknown/unverifiable). No rate limit — the custom-message dialog is an unthrottled plaintext write path to the partner's notification tray. No DDL means no staging environment can run this feature at all.
modules.scale_reason: Backend object is not reproducible from source (no DDL, no RLS in repo), full 50-row refetch on every event, and an unbounded per-message pg_net → edge function → FCM chain with no batching or throttle.

modules.name: Rituals
modules.purpose: Advertised as scheduled recurring couple moments ('goodnight', 'goodmorning', 'weekly high/low', custom) delivered at a chosen time.
modules.tables: rituals (schema.sql:70-78: couple_id, type, cron, message, deliver_at, delivered) + index rituals_pending_idx on (delivered, deliver_at)
modules.realtime_or_push: NONE. No realtime channel, no push, no cron job, no edge function.
modules.current_mechanism: CreateRitualSheet builds deliverAt as DateTime(today, chosen HH:MM) in device local time (create_ritual_screen.dart:38-44), converts to UTC and INSERTs. RitualRepository.list() reads them back ordered by deliver_at. That is the entire feature. The repository comment states it outright (ritual_repository.dart:6-9): 'v1 does not schedule push notifications'. Nothing ever sets delivered=true; the `cron` column is never written.
modules.known_weaknesses: This is a feature that never fires. The UI says 'This ritual will no longer be scheduled' on delete and renders a 'delivered' badge that can never appear. rituals_screen.dart:273-274 prints DateFormat(deliverAt.toLocal()) TWICE and labels the second copy '· HH:MM their time' — the partner's timezone is never applied, so the 'their time' readout is always wrong for any couple not in the same zone (i.e. the entire target market). Picking a time earlier than now creates a row already in the past.
modules.scale_reason: Harmless today because nothing runs, but the moment delivery is implemented it needs a scheduler that scans rituals across all couples per minute and honours per-user timezones — an architecture that does not exist anywhere in this codebase (there is no worker, no pg_cron job for rituals, no queue).

modules.name: Games hub
modules.purpose: Menu of three couple mini-games.
modules.tables: none
modules.realtime_or_push: none
modules.current_mechanism: Static list of three cards routed to /app/games/truth-dare, /app/games/would-you-rather, /app/games/never-have-i-ever. Card copy switches on contentLanguageProvider (English / Roman Urdu).
modules.known_weaknesses: The hub labels Truth or Dare `synced: true` (LIVE badge) and marks Would You Rather / Never Have I Ever `synced: false` — but all three sync over broadcast channels. The badge is decorative and wrong. No age gate on this route despite Truth or Dare carrying an explicit 'Spicy' tier (see below).
modules.scale_reason: Pure static UI.

modules.name: Truth or Dare (synced)
modules.purpose: Turn-based Truth or Dare with three heat tiers, same card on both phones.
modules.tables: NONE — nothing about a game is ever persisted server-side. Local state only: SharedPreferences keys `nrb_td_<type>_<tier>_<lang>` via NoRepeatBag.
modules.realtime_or_push: Supabase Realtime BROADCAST channel `game_td:<coupleId>`, events 'state' and 'sync' (truth_dare_screen.dart:56-67). Ephemeral — nothing is stored, nothing is replayed. No push.
modules.current_mechanism: Whole game state (turn uid, round, tier, card {type,tier,index}) lives in each client's setState and is re-broadcast on every mutation. On subscribe, a 900ms timer sends a 'sync' ping; whoever is already started re-broadcasts their state. Cards travel as a POOL INDEX, not text, so each phone renders from its own language pool (localiseTD). Pools are built combinatorially (5 openers × 21 cores per tier per type per language, game_content.dart:303-312).
modules.known_weaknesses: Requires both partners in the same screen at the same instant on a live websocket — no state survives a backgrounded app, a dropped socket, or one partner arriving 10 seconds later. Two clients both tapping Start produce two conflicting turn owners with no arbitration. The cross-language index contract is an unenforced invariant: if anyone adds an English opener without an Urdu one, every card silently desyncs. The broadcast channel is NOT a private/authorized channel (no RealtimeChannelConfig anywhere in the client, no realtime.messages RLS in any .sql) — any authenticated user who knows a couple_id can join `game_td:<coupleId>` and read or inject cards. couple_id is not secret; it is the first path segment of every public couple_media URL. The 'Spicy' tier is reachable at /app/games/truth-dare with no isAdult check and no modest_mode check, unlike the Closer tab which gates on both (app_shell.dart:215-221).
modules.scale_reason: Broadcast is cheap per message but unauthorized channels are a cross-couple confidentiality hole that gets worse with user count, and NoRepeatBag persists every dealt SENTENCE (not an index) into SharedPreferences — thousands of strings across 12 tier/type/language bags.

modules.name: Never Have I Ever / Would You Rather (synced card game)
modules.purpose: One card on both phones, either partner can deal the next, with a live answer strip.
modules.tables: none. SharedPreferences bags `nrb_card_<deck>_<lang>`.
modules.realtime_or_push: Broadcast channel `gcard:<deckKey>:<coupleId>`, events 'card' and 'sync'. Ephemeral, no persistence, no push.
modules.current_mechanism: Identical shape to Truth or Dare: draw locally from NoRepeatBag, broadcast {from, text, index}, receiver looks the index up in its own language pool and marks it seen locally so the no-repeat bag stays roughly shared.
modules.known_weaknesses: Same as Truth or Dare: both-online-simultaneously requirement, unauthorized public broadcast channel keyed on a guessable couple_id, no server state. The no-repeat 'shared' bag is only shared while both are on screen — a card dealt while the partner is away is never retired on their device.
modules.scale_reason: Same unauthorized-broadcast exposure; message volume is low (one per deal).

modules.name: In-game chat panel
modules.purpose: Live answer strip embedded in every game.
modules.tables: NONE — messages are never stored anywhere, not even locally.
modules.realtime_or_push: Broadcast channel `gchat:<gameKey>:<coupleId>`, event 'msg'.
modules.current_mechanism: Text goes into an in-memory List<_GameMsg> and out as a broadcast payload {from, name, text}. Closing the screen destroys the conversation.
modules.known_weaknesses: Real user messages (including the sender's display name) travel over a public, unauthorized broadcast channel keyed only on couple_id — readable by any authenticated user who guesses/derives the id. Nothing is delivered to a partner who is not on that exact screen at that exact moment; there is no 'you missed this'. The empty-state hint is hardcoded Roman Urdu regardless of the language toggle.
modules.scale_reason: Confidentiality of plaintext user content on an unauthenticated channel; volume itself is small.

modules.name: Pick For Us (consent dice)
modules.purpose: Three-tier 'let the dice decide' with per-tier dual consent.
modules.tables: dice_rolls (couple_id, rolled_at, tier, result_tags[]), dice_tier_consents (couple_id, tier, user_id, granted, granted_at) — both in intimacy_tables.sql with couple-scoped RLS.
modules.realtime_or_push: NONE. No realtime channel, no push.
modules.current_mechanism: On open, fetchConsents() reads every dice_tier_consents row for the couple into a {tier → {uid → bool}} map; a tier is 'unlocked' only if both uids are true. Tapping consent upserts my row then re-reads the whole consent set and returns the pair. Rolling picks a random tag per enabled tier client-side (Random in the repository) and INSERTs a dice_rolls row.
modules.known_weaknesses: Consent is polled, not pushed: partner A granting consent is invisible to partner B until B closes and reopens the screen, so the 'waiting for them' state can be stale indefinitely. dice_rolls has no author column and the RLS is couple-wide, so either partner can insert rolls at any tier regardless of the consent state (consent is enforced only in the Dart UI). Randomness is per-device, so the two phones never see the same roll unless one of them refetches.
modules.scale_reason: Tiny write volume; the defects are correctness/consent, not throughput.

modules.name: Rapid camera (in-app camera)
modules.purpose: Fast camera with live filters, pinch zoom, screen-flash selfies, hold-to-record video, one-tap send to chat, and 'Use Photo' return mode for the Home check-in.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/chat/rapid_camera_screen.dart (route /app/rapid-camera; nav index 2 in app_shell.dart:296-303 and Home's check-in), camera_bake.dart, camera_filters.dart, camera_filter_painter.dart
modules.tables: messages (via ChatRepository), storage couple_media (images, PUBLIC bucket), storage couple_intimate (videos, private + signed URLs)
modules.realtime_or_push: After upload, ChatSendQueue fires ChatBroadcastService.broadcastImage on the chat broadcast channel as a fast path; the durable delivery is the messages INSERT + its postgres_changes echo + the notify_message() → reach-notify FCM push.
modules.current_mechanism: Explicit Permission.camera/microphone request before creating the controller (with MilesApp.systemOverlayActive set so the disguise cover does not fire). Controller ladder veryHigh → high with a 12s init timeout. Capture writes the plugin's JPEG; if the filter is 'none' and no mirror is needed the sensor JPEG is shipped untouched, otherwise a compute() isolate decodes, mirrors by raw row reversal, applies the 4×5 matrix/blur/overlay/grain and re-encodes at q88 capped at 1920px (camera_bake.dart). Send hands the File to the in-memory ChatSendQueue singleton and pops immediately.
modules.known_weaknesses: ChatSendQueue is a RAM-only singleton (chat_send_queue.dart:51) — a pending upload does not survive process death, and Android will kill a backgrounded Flutter process mid-upload; the photo and its temp file are then gone with no record and no retry. Failed sends are only recoverable while the process lives. Images land in a PUBLIC bucket with a never-expiring URL (getPublicUrl), while videos correctly use the private bucket — an inconsistent privacy posture in an app built around concealment.
modules.scale_reason: Every photo is a full-resolution JPEG upload to Supabase Storage with no server-side resize/derivative pipeline and no CDN cache policy in the repo; storage cost and egress scale linearly with users and nothing ever prunes couple_media except explicit message deletion.

modules.name: Media viewer
modules.purpose: Full-screen pinch-zoom viewer for chat photos and the Home check-in snap, with a 'save to vault' button.
modules.tables: none directly; writes via SaveMediaService → personal_vault_items
modules.realtime_or_push: none
modules.current_mechanism: A plain Image.network(url) inside an InteractiveViewer with a Hero. No auth header, no signed URL — it only works because couple_media is a public bucket.
modules.known_weaknesses: Uses raw Image.network rather than the app's own cached NetImage, so every open re-downloads the full-resolution original and decodes it at source size into the image cache (NetImage exists precisely to avoid this, net_image.dart:26-40). It cannot display anything from the private couple_intimate bucket. senderName defaults to the literal string 'a message', which becomes the vault label ('Photo from a message').
modules.scale_reason: Client-side memory/bandwidth waste per view, not a backend bottleneck.

modules.name: Saved media / Personal Vault
modules.purpose: PIN- or biometric-locked personal space for private notes and 'saved' chat media, advertised as writing zero bytes to the device.
modules.tables: personal_vault_items (private_vault.sql:26-36, owner-only RLS), vault_pin (bcrypt hash + failed_attempts + locked_until); RPCs set_vault_pin / verify_vault_pin / has_vault_pin
modules.realtime_or_push: none — plain fetch on open.
modules.current_mechanism: 'Saving' media does NOT copy any bytes: it inserts a row whose `content` is either the public couple_media URL verbatim or the string 'intimate:<storagePath>', with the human label crammed into the `media_url` column (vault_repository.dart:87-94). Opening an item resolves a fresh signed URL for the intimate path, then hands the URL to launchUrl(..., LaunchMode.externalApplication) — i.e. the system browser (vault_screen.dart:92-93). PIN verification is server-side bcrypt with a 5-try/15-minute lockout; the gate re-locks on every non-resumed lifecycle state.
modules.known_weaknesses: A saved item is a pointer the OTHER partner can revoke: delete_message_for_everyone and clear_conversation_everyone delete the storage object (chat_media_cleanup.sql:25-27, 44-50), so the vault entry silently 404s afterwards — the promise 'saved forever, privately' is not kept. Opening saved media launches the EXTERNAL BROWSER, dumping a private (often intimate) image into Chrome's history/cache on a phone whose whole point is that the app is disguised — this defeats both the PIN gate and the disguise. The 'label' is stored in the media_url column, so the schema no longer means what it says. couple_media URLs are public and permanent, so vault 'privacy' for photos is a UI convention only.
modules.scale_reason: Low write volume, but the dangling-reference model means vault contents rot at a rate proportional to message deletion, and there is no reference counting or copy-on-save anywhere.

modules.name: App lock (biometric/PIN gate over the whole app)
modules.purpose: Require fingerprint/face/PIN to open the app.
modules.tables: none — SharedPreferences keys `app_lock_enabled`, `app_lock_pin_hash`
modules.realtime_or_push: none
modules.current_mechanism: local_auth for biometrics (MainActivity extends FlutterFragmentActivity so the prompt works), plus a mandatory 4-digit fallback PIN stored as sha256('miles-applock::' + pin) in SharedPreferences (app_lock.dart:36-48).
modules.known_weaknesses: Unsalted, un-stretched SHA-256 of a 4-digit PIN in plaintext SharedPreferences XML: the whole 10,000-entry rainbow table is computable in milliseconds from any device backup or rooted read. No attempt counter and no lockout on the app-lock PIN (unlike the vault PIN, which is bcrypt + server-side lockout). The two PIN systems are unrelated and a user can end up with two different 4-digit PINs.
modules.scale_reason: Entirely local; a security defect rather than a scaling one.

modules.name: Cycle tracking
modules.purpose: Period logging + prediction for the female partner, with an opt-in gentle summary card for the male partner.
modules.tables: cycle_settings (user_id, couple_id, avg_cycle_length, avg_period_length, share_with_partner, tracking_enabled, on_period_now, updated_at) and cycle_events (user_id, couple_id, type, event_date, created_at) — NEITHER TABLE HAS DDL IN E:/LDR/supabase. Sensitive health data whose RLS posture cannot be verified from source.
modules.realtime_or_push: postgres_changes on `cycle_events` with NO couple_id filter — cycle_screen.dart:66-74 and partner_cycle_card.dart:40-48 both subscribe to the whole table and simply re-run _load() on any event. No push.
modules.current_mechanism: setOnPeriod() inserts a cycle_events row with event_date = the DEVICE's local calendar date (cycle_repository.dart:237) and upserts on_period_now on cycle_settings. All prediction is client-side: CyclePrediction.compute averages start-to-start gaps (10<gap<90) and derives phase from dayOfCycle vs (cycleLen-14). The male view fetches the partner's settings, and only if share_with_partner is true fetches her events and derives a detail-free card.
modules.known_weaknesses: Backend tables do not exist in version control — the app's most sensitive data has no reviewable RLS. Both subscriptions are unfiltered table-wide listeners (correctness depends entirely on RLS filtering realtime, which cannot be confirmed here). cycle_screen's _subscribe uses the known-bad `_channel?.unsubscribe()` then immediately re-`channel()` with the same topic on every realtimeResumed — the exact duplicate-topic 'joined but dead' bug that ManagedSubscription was written to fix and which the rest of the app now uses. Views are gated on profile.gender: a user who never sets gender falls into the male branch and sees the 'partner' view of themselves. Dates come from the device clock, so a wrong clock silently corrupts the history.
modules.scale_reason: Unfiltered postgres_changes subscriptions on a table with thousands of users mean Realtime evaluates RLS per subscriber per change; two such subscriptions are mounted (Home card + screen). Combined with no DDL/no index guarantees and no server-side prediction, this is the module least ready for multi-tenant load.

modules.name: Love notes (pooled)
modules.purpose: Serve the male partner a never-repeating romantic paragraph to edit and send into chat.
modules.tables: none server-side — sends land in `messages` via ChatRepository.sendText. Local state in SharedPreferences (`love_notes_sent_indices`, `love_notes_shuffle_order`, `love_note_recipient_name`).
modules.realtime_or_push: n/a (the resulting chat message uses the normal chat path).
modules.current_mechanism: 250 hardcoded const Dart strings (Roman Urdu/Punjabi, husband→wife voice) compiled into the APK.
