LoveNotesTracker keeps a shuffled index order and a used-index list in SharedPreferences, reshuffling once the pool is exhausted. 155 of the notes carry a {name} token filled by renderLoveNote from a locally stored recipient name.
modules.known_weaknesses: The entry point is DEAD: FeatureFlags.pooledLoveNotes is false (feature_flags.dart:15) so the button never renders — but the 250-paragraph pool still ships in every APK. The content is one specific couple's private register with hardcoded pet names ('begum', 'churail', 'bandri', 'chuii') and no localisation, and is gender-hardcoded husband→wife. The used-index list grows to 250 entries in SharedPreferences per device.
modules.scale_reason: Flag-disabled dead code with zero backend footprint; the only cost is APK size and the product risk if the flag is ever flipped as-is.

modules.name: Breath sync
modules.purpose: Shared 4-7-8 breathing pacer — both phones pulse in unison.
modules.tables: breath_events (breath_events.sql: couple_id, user_id, started_at bigint ms-since-epoch, created_at) with a pg_cron nightly delete of rows older than 1 day.
modules.realtime_or_push: postgres_changes INSERT on breath_events filtered by couple_id, via ManagedSubscription. No push.
modules.current_mechanism: Tapping Begin INSERTs a row carrying the DEVICE's DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch. The partner's client receives the insert, computes elapsedMs = its own DateTime.now() minus the received started_at, ignores the event if elapsedMs > one full cycle (19s), otherwise starts its animation at that offset. At the end of every cycle _beginCycle() recurses — inserting ANOTHER row — so an active session writes one DB row per user per 19 seconds indefinitely, and each of those rows fans out over Realtime to the partner, who restarts their own cycle (and their own recursive insert).
modules.known_weaknesses: Sync is computed from two unsynchronised device clocks even though ServerClock exists and is used elsewhere — a phone more than 19 seconds off will discard every partner event and never sync, silently, with the UI still saying 'they'll feel it the moment they arrive'. There is no Stop broadcast: pressing Stop cancels only the local timer, so the partner keeps breathing alone. The insert-per-cycle design uses a durable Postgres table for what is a pure ephemeral tick (the file's own comment calls it 'a tiny table so the realtime channel can fan out').
modules.scale_reason: ~3 INSERTs/user/minute plus a Realtime fan-out and a full trigger/WAL cycle per tick, for data with a 19-second useful life, retained a full day. A broadcast channel would cost zero writes. 1,000 concurrent breathers = 3,000 durable writes/min.

modules.name: Reach (hold-to-reach alert)
modules.purpose: Send a partner an urgent full-screen 'reaching for you' alert that can wake their screen.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/mobile/lib/features/reach/reach_button.dart (on Home), reach_repository.dart, reach_overlay_screen.dart; app-wide listener in app_shell.dart:112-182; E:/LDR/mobile/lib/core/services/reach_notifications.dart; E:/LDR/supabase/functions/reach-notify/index.ts
modules.tables: reach_events (couple_id, from_user, created_at, acknowledged_at, expires_at default now()+30s; replica identity full; in the supabase_realtime publication). reach_pulses ALSO EXISTS (reach_pulses.sql, with its own pg_cron cleanup) but NO CLIENT CODE EVER READS OR WRITES IT — a dead table.
modules.realtime_or_push: Both. Foreground: postgres_changes INSERT on reach_events filtered by couple_id, subscribed app-wide in AppShell. Background: AFTER INSERT trigger notify_reach() → pg_net POST → reach-notify edge function → OAuth2 service-account JWT → FCM v1 data-only message with ttl 30s → firebaseMessagingBackgroundHandler builds a full-screen-intent notification.
modules.current_mechanism: INSERT one row; both delivery paths are de-duplicated in AppShell._showReach by reach id. Acknowledge is a client UPDATE stamping acknowledged_at.
modules.known_weaknesses: AppShell._onReach drops any event where !e.isActive, and isActive compares the SERVER-generated expires_at against the local DateTime.now() (reach_repository.dart:29) — a device clock running 30+ seconds fast discards every reach it receives, silently, forever. The 30s cooldown is client-only, held in widget state (reach_button.dart:20-28), so it resets on navigation and is trivially bypassed via the REST API — an unrate-limited path to wake someone's screen. profiles.fcm_token is a single column, so a second device overwrites the first and only the newest device is ever notified. FCM ttl is 30s, so a doze-stuck delivery is discarded. reach-notify returns 200 on every failure to avoid retry storms, and pg_net swallows responses, so silent delivery failures are only visible in net._http_response.
modules.scale_reason: Every reach is a Postgres INSERT + trigger + pg_net HTTP call + edge function cold start + Google OAuth token exchange (the token is minted per invocation, never cached, functions/reach-notify/index.ts:51-90) + FCM send. That is a full OAuth round trip per notification for every reach, care nudge, call and CHAT MESSAGE in the system — the single hardest bottleneck in the push path.

modules.name: Settings
modules.purpose: Profile, avatar, gender, timezone, content language, disguise, location sharing mode, FSI permission, modest mode, biometric app lock, remove partner, sign out, delete account.
modules.tables: profiles (display_name, status_message, gender, timezone, avatar_url), couples.modest_mode, presence.location_sharing_mode, storage couple_media (avatars/), RPCs leave_couple() and delete_my_account()
modules.realtime_or_push: none; reads sessionProvider and re-runs loadProfile() after each write.
modules.current_mechanism: Direct table writes through SupabaseRepository plus two SECURITY DEFINER RPCs. Avatar upload goes to the PUBLIC couple_media bucket with getPublicUrl. Location mode writes presence.location_sharing_mode and then does one immediate shareOnce. Delete account clears the FCM token, calls delete_my_account() and signs out.
modules.known_weaknesses: Modest mode is a single boolean on `couples` written by whichever partner flips the switch (supabase_repository.dart:128-135), so 'This reveals the intimacy module for both of you' and the schema comment 'both must opt out to reveal it' (intimacy_additions.sql) are both false — one partner unilaterally reveals it for the other. There are NO notification preferences anywhere: a user cannot mute reaches, care nudges or messages. There is no cycle-tracking entry (it lives only behind the drawer/Home card). Every profile save triggers a full loadProfile() which re-fetches profile + couple + partner (3 queries). Avatars go to a public, never-expiring URL.
modules.scale_reason: Low traffic; the risks are consent-model and product-gap, not throughput.

modules.name: Ads
modules.purpose: AdMob banner monetisation.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/mobile/lib/core/ads/ad_config.dart, ad_service.dart, banner_ad_slot.dart; single mount point app_shell.dart:241 (Touch tab only); AdService.init() at main.dart:80
modules.tables: none
modules.realtime_or_push: none
modules.current_mechanism: AdConfig.adsEnabled is hardcoded false and AdConfig.useTestAds is hardcoded true; the three production unit IDs are the literal strings 'REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_BANNER_UNIT_ID' etc. BannerAdSlot._load() returns immediately when adsEnabled is false, so no ad is ever requested. AdService.init() still initialises the Google Mobile Ads SDK on every cold start.
modules.known_weaknesses: The module produces zero revenue and cannot without a code change. The SDK is still initialised and google_mobile_ads is still a dependency, which pulls the Android AD_ID permission into the manifest and therefore onto the Play Data Safety form for a feature that does nothing. Banner is placed only on the Touch tab.
modules.scale_reason: Inert. Note for redesign: monetisation is currently a stub, not a revenue path.

modules.name: Daily prompt
modules.purpose: One shared question per day; both answers revealed once both have responded.
modules.tables: daily_prompts (couple_id, prompt_text, scheduled_date, unique(couple_id, scheduled_date)), prompt_responses (prompt_id, user_id, response_text, unique(prompt_id,user_id)) — both in schema.sql with explicit RLS.
modules.realtime_or_push: none — pure fetch on open.
modules.current_mechanism: ensureToday() takes the DEVICE's local calendar date, SELECTs a daily_prompts row for (couple_id, that date), and if absent INSERTs one whose text is promptPool[dayOfYear % 20]. Answers are upserted into prompt_responses.
modules.known_weaknesses: This breaks on exactly the users it is built for. Two partners in different timezones produce two DIFFERENT scheduled_date values for the same evening, so each creates and answers their OWN daily_prompts row and neither ever sees the other's answer — the reveal never happens. If both open it at the same moment in the same timezone, both INSERT and the loser hits the unique constraint through .single(), which throws an unhandled PostgrestException. Pool is 20 prompts on a 365-day modulus, so the same question recurs roughly every 20 days forever.
modules.scale_reason: Correctness failure that scales with timezone diversity (i.e. with the target market), plus an insert race with no upsert/on-conflict handling.

modules.name: Reasons ('reasons I love you' jar)
modules.purpose: Shared list of reasons, one featured per day.
modules.tables: love_reasons (couple_id, author, text, created_at) — NO DDL ANYWHERE IN E:/LDR/supabase. RLS unverifiable from source.
modules.realtime_or_push: postgres_changes (all events) on love_reasons filtered by couple_id via ManagedSubscription; full list refetch on any change. No push.
modules.current_mechanism: Plain insert/select/delete of plaintext rows, ordered created_at DESC with no limit. The 'featured' reason is _reasons[dayOfYear % _reasons.length] computed from the device date over the DESC-ordered list.
modules.known_weaknesses: Backend object missing from version control. The featured pick is computed over a list whose ordering shifts every time anyone adds a reason, so 'today's reason' changes mid-day; and because it uses the local device date, the two partners can see different featured reasons on the same day. The list query has no limit — a couple with a thousand reasons refetches all of them on every realtime event.
modules.scale_reason: Unbounded SELECT re-run on every insert/delete, plus a table with no committed schema or index.

modules.name: Timeline / visits
modules.purpose: Countdown to the next visit and a history of past visits.
modules.tables: visits (schema.sql:41-50, couple-scoped RLS, indexed on (couple_id,is_upcoming,start_date)). visit_memories exists in schema.sql with full RLS but is NEVER referenced by any client code — a dead table.
modules.realtime_or_push: none — fetch on didChangeDependencies.
modules.current_mechanism: SELECT * from visits ordered by start_date; the screen computes the countdown from DateTime.now() locally and renders past/future sections.
modules.known_weaknesses: No realtime, so a visit added by one partner is invisible to the other until they reopen the screen. Countdown is device-clock based and uses no partner timezone. The photo-memories half of the feature (visit_memories) was schema'd and RLS'd but never built.
modules.scale_reason: Small bounded reads, properly indexed.

modules.name: Together (shared presence room)
modules.purpose: Two avatars in a shared space that lean together and emit hearts/kisses when either taps.
modules.tables: presence.avatar_emoji only (read via fetchMine/fetchPartner, written via PresenceService.setAvatarEmoji).
modules.realtime_or_push: Broadcast channel `together:<coupleId>`, event 'moment'. Ephemeral.
modules.current_mechanism: Each tap sends {action} on the broadcast channel and plays the animation locally; the receiver plays the same animation. Nothing is stored.
modules.known_weaknesses: Requires both partners on the screen simultaneously with a live socket; nothing arrives otherwise and there is no indication it was missed. Unauthorized broadcast channel keyed on couple_id (same exposure as the games). Avatar emoji is fetched once on init and never re-read, so a partner changing theirs is not reflected until reopen.
modules.scale_reason: Low message volume, but shares the unauthorized-channel exposure.

modules.name: Watch Together
modules.purpose: Paste a YouTube link and keep play/pause/seek loosely synced on both phones.
modules.tables: none — nothing is persisted, not even the current video.
modules.realtime_or_push: Broadcast channel `watch:<coupleId>`, event 'watch', plus an unconditional 2500ms Timer.periodic that re-broadcasts {videoId, playing, positionMs} (watch_together_screen.dart:48).
modules.current_mechanism: youtube_player_flutter drives playback locally; a 2.5s heartbeat plus a play/pause listener push state; the receiver seeks only when drift exceeds 2500ms and suppresses echo with a 600ms _applyingRemote flag.
modules.known_weaknesses: Position is compared as raw player positions with no clock/latency compensation, so the tolerated drift is up to ~2.5s by design and network latency is never subtracted. Both users touching controls produces an oscillation the 600ms guard only partially damps. Nothing survives leaving the screen — no 'resume where we were'. Unauthorized broadcast channel keyed on couple_id. YouTube ToS around synchronised third-party playback is not addressed anywhere.
modules.scale_reason: 24 broadcast messages per user per minute while watching (48 per couple), continuous for the length of a film — the highest sustained broadcast rate in the app after Heartbeat.

modules.name: Heartbeat (PPG pulse sharing)
modules.purpose: Measure the user's pulse with the camera+torch and let the partner feel each beat as a haptic.
modules.tables: none — no BPM is ever stored.
modules.realtime_or_push: Broadcast channel `heartbeat:<coupleId>`, event 'hb'. One message PER DETECTED BEAT (heartbeat_screen.dart:177) plus one per BPM update plus one on stop.
modules.current_mechanism: CameraController at ResolutionPreset.low with the torch on, startImageStream, luma-plane mean sampled every 16th byte, fed to PpgDetector which emits onBeat/onBpm. Each callback fires a broadcast; the receiver triggers HapticFeedback.lightImpact() per beat.
modules.known_weaknesses: Requires both partners in the screen simultaneously on a live socket. Raw biometric data (heart rate) travels over an UNAUTHORIZED public broadcast channel keyed on couple_id — anyone who knows the id can read it. No consent gate on either side. Camera+torch at full duty cycle is a battery and thermal load; the lifecycle guard exists precisely because it previously kept the torch lit behind the disguise cover.
modules.scale_reason: ~70-90 broadcast messages per user per minute — by far the highest realtime message rate in the app. 100 concurrent pairs ≈ 15,000 Realtime messages/minute for a feature with zero durable value, and Supabase bills broadcast messages.

modules.name: Time capsules + proximity unlock
modules.purpose: Sealed collection of notes/photos/voice that unlocks on a date, on physical proximity, or both.
modules.tables: capsules, capsule_items (capsules.sql, with a sealed-until-unlocked SELECT policy), storage bucket capsule-media (private, folder-scoped policies). RPCs capsule_seal_summary(uuid), unlock_capsule(uuid).
modules.realtime_or_push: postgres_changes on `capsules` (in the realtime publication); proximity uses an EPHEMERAL broadcast channel with a 4s ping timer (proximity_service.dart:107). capsule_list_screen also runs a 30s poll timer.
modules.current_mechanism: Items are un-SELECTable until capsules.unlocked_at is set. unlock_capsule() is SECURITY DEFINER and validates the date for modes 'date' and 'both'. Proximity is computed entirely client-side: each phone broadcasts its own coarse position on a realtime channel every 4s and both compute the Haversine distance locally; no coordinate is ever persisted.
modules.known_weaknesses: For unlock_mode='proximity' the RPC performs NO check at all (capsules.sql:87-92 only branches on 'date' and 'both') — any couple member can call unlock_capsule directly and open a proximity capsule from anywhere. The proximity broadcast channel is unauthorized like every other broadcast channel here, so live coarse coordinates are readable by anyone who knows the couple_id. Both phones must be in the screen at the same moment for a proximity unlock to ever trigger.
modules.scale_reason: 4s position pings per user while the screen is open, a 30s list poll, and a server-side seal whose central promise (proximity) is enforced only in Dart.

modules.name: Fake News cover (disguise front screen)
modules.purpose: The 'News' app the launcher disguise shows; must look genuine.
modules.tables: none — a static in-memory cache (RssService.cached / cachedAt).
modules.realtime_or_push: none. Plain HTTPS GET.
modules.current_mechanism: Sequentially fetches three public RSS feeds (feeds.bbci.co.uk, aljazeera.com, feeds.npr.org) with a spoofed 'Mozilla/5.0' User-Agent and a 6s timeout each, parses XML, sorts by pubDate, keeps 30 items in a static field that survives screen rebuilds.
modules.known_weaknesses: Three unpaid third-party endpoints fetched directly from every user's device with a spoofed UA — BBC/NPR/Al Jazeera will rate-limit or block by IP/UA at volume, and the cover screen then renders empty, which is exactly when the disguise fails. Fetches are sequential, so a slow feed adds up to 18s before content appears. No disk cache, no ETag, no stale-while-revalidate.
modules.scale_reason: Direct client fan-out to third-party feeds that have no agreement with this app; needs a server-side cached feed proxy before thousands of devices poll them.

modules.name: App shell, navigation and screen-presence publishing
modules.purpose: Bottom-nav container, app-wide Reach/call listeners, realtime reconnection, and publishing 'which screen am I on' to the partner.
modules.tables: presence.current_screen (durable fallback)
modules.realtime_or_push: Broadcast channel `screen_presence:<coupleId>` (events 'screen' and 'warm') for sub-second sync, backed by a presence-table write for durability. Plus the app-wide reach_events postgres_changes subscription.
modules.current_mechanism: A NavigatorObserver reports every push/pop/replace, and AppShell calls publishActiveTab() on tab changes (tabs are setState, not routes). Each report broadcasts the screen name AND upserts presence.current_screen with isAppActivity:true. On every AppLifecycleState.resumed, AppShell calls realtime.disconnect() then realtime.connect() (app_shell.dart:70-80), and the resulting onOpen fans out through realtimeResumed so every ManagedSubscription tears its channel down (awaited removeChannel) and rebuilds it.
modules.known_weaknesses: Every navigation is a database write, and the app has 44 routes — browsing the drawer generates a presence UPSERT per screen. The forced full-socket disconnect/reconnect on every foreground means every mounted subscription in the app rejoins at once. Three modules (notably cycle_screen.dart:64-75) still use the old unsubscribe()+re-channel() pattern instead of ManagedSubscription and can leave duplicate-topic dead channels.
modules.scale_reason: A per-navigation write amplification pattern plus a per-foreground socket storm. Thousands of users backgrounding/foregrounding produce synchronized reconnect + rejoin bursts against Supabase Realtime, which is exactly the load pattern that causes channel-join throttling.

modules.name: Push fan-in (reach-notify edge function)
modules.purpose: Single edge function that turns reach, care, call and message inserts into FCM notifications.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/supabase/functions/reach-notify/index.ts; triggers in fcm_push.sql (reach), 20260628_care_call_push.sql (care, call), message_push.sql (message); client side E:/LDR/mobile/lib/core/services/fcm_service.dart and core/services/reach_notifications.dart
modules.tables: profiles.fcm_token / fcm_token_updated_at; reads profiles to resolve the recipient (couple_id = X and id <> sender, limit 1)
modules.realtime_or_push: FCM HTTP v1, data-only messages so the Android background isolate builds the notification wearing the current disguise.
modules.current_mechanism: Four AFTER INSERT triggers each perform net.http_post to the same function with {kind, record}. The function mints a fresh RS256 service-account JWT and exchanges it at oauth2.googleapis.com for an access token ON EVERY INVOCATION, looks up the recipient's single fcm_token, resolves the sender name, and posts to FCM with ttl 30s (86400s for messages). Unregistered tokens are nulled out. Every failure path returns HTTP 200.
modules.known_weaknesses: No token caching: one Google OAuth round trip per notification. One fcm_token column per user means multi-device is impossible — a second install silently steals notifications from the first. pg_net is fire-and-forget and discards the response, so the only diagnostic is net._http_response (documented in message_push.sql). Returning 200 on every error means monitoring sees a healthy function while delivery is 100% failing. Every notification body is a generic disguise string with no content, so push conveys 'something happened' and nothing more.
modules.scale_reason: Every single user-visible event in the app (every chat message, reach, nudge, call) becomes: trigger → pg_net HTTP → edge function cold start → OAuth token exchange → profiles lookup ×2 → FCM POST. At thousands of users this saturates pg_net's worker queue and Google's token endpoint quota; it needs batching, a cached token, and a proper worker/queue rather than per-row HTTP from Postgres.

modules.name: Schema management / backend reproducibility
modules.purpose: How the Postgres schema and buckets are defined and deployed.
modules.entry_points: E:/LDR/supabase/*.sql (43 loose files), E:/LDR/supabase/.temp/linked-project.json; no supabase/migrations/, no config.toml, no seed
modules.tables: All of them. Client-referenced tables with NO DDL in the repo: care_nudges, cycle_settings, cycle_events, love_reasons. Storage buckets with no DDL: couple_media, couple_intimate, chat-bg (only capsule-media is created, capsules.sql:110). SQL-defined tables no client ever touches: reach_pulses, visit_memories, mood_lamp, consent_state, couple_dissolutions, fantasy_jar_reveals.
modules.realtime_or_push: n/a
modules.current_mechanism: Ordered-by-header-comment .sql files applied by hand in the Supabase SQL editor (several files say so in their headers), plus out-of-band DDL applied via MCP. Later files patch earlier ones (hardening_2026_08.sql, hardening_couple_id_fix.sql, newuser_fixes.sql) rather than superseding them, so the true schema is the union of 43 files applied in an order recorded nowhere machine-readable.
modules.known_weaknesses: A fresh Supabase project cannot be rebuilt from this directory — four live tables and three buckets have no definition, so a staging environment silently loses Care, Cycle and Reasons and gets an unknown storage/RLS posture. The RLS protecting the app's most sensitive data (menstrual cycle history) is unverifiable from source. Dead client code calls a dropped function: SupabaseRepository.joinCouple invokes join_couple_by_code, which hardening_2026_08.sql:85 drops.
modules.scale_reason: No reproducible environment means no staging, no reviewable RLS change, no rollback and no disaster recovery. Every other scaling fix in this list is gated on fixing this first.

cross_cutting.notes:
PATTERNS THAT REPEAT — GOOD

1. SECURITY DEFINER RPCs as the only write path for anything privileged. create_pairing_invite, redeem_pairing_invite, leave_couple, delete_my_account, hide_message, clear_conversation all run as owner and gate internally on auth.uid(). The client never writes couple_id through the table API. This is the strongest structural decision in the codebase and it should survive the redesign.

2. Column-level privilege control done correctly, eventually. hardening_couple_id_fix.sql documents that a column REVOKE is a no-op against a table-level GRANT, and rebuilds the grant list from information_schema (hardening_couple_id_fix.sql l.28-43). The same block is repeated in hardening_2026_08.sql l.35-46 and newuser_fixes.sql l.162-173. Paired with trg_guard_couple_id declared SECURITY INVOKER on purpose so current_user is the real writer.

3. Server-authoritative timestamps where they were found to matter. presence_server_time.sql moves app_last_active_at onto now() in a BEFORE trigger; receipts_v2.sql did the same for read receipts.

4. Deliberate non-enumeration. Password reset returns an identical message either way; the biometric prompt is nameless ("Verify it's you", app_lock.dart l.94); MaterialApp.title is '' in both branches so recents shows the alias; pushes are data-only so the sender cannot learn the recipient's disguise.

PATTERNS THAT REPEAT — BAD

5. The migration set is a stack of hand-applied patches with no ordering guarantee and no migration runner. E:/LDR/supabase/*.sql is 43 loose files; leave_couple() is defined three times (settings_and_delete.sql → 20260627_leave_couple_fix.sql → 20260628_leave_couple_privacy.sql), create_pairing_invite twice (pairing_invites.sql → newuser_fixes.sql), create_couple twice, presence_stamp_server_time twice (presence_server_time.sql → newuser_fixes.sql l.124-140). The repo ships verify_applied.sql and four diagnose_*.sql files precisely because nothing else can tell you what state a database is in. profiles.gender and profiles.gender_set exist in production only because newuser_fixes.sql l.152-153 finally created them after the code had been shipping against them. Any new environment is a new outage.

6. Every onboarding stage is a redirect trap with a bolted-on escape hatch. router.dart forces /welcome, then /couple, then /role-setup, from EVERY other path. Each screen grew a Sign-out button after it stranded someone: couple_page.dart l.166-174 ("This screen is a trap otherwise"), role_setup_screen.dart l.22-25 ("One failure and the account was unusable forever"). /welcome still has none. This is a design pattern, not three bugs.

7. Client-clock dependence persists in the places nobody audited. The server-side fix landed for presence and receipts, but: activePairingInvite filters expires_at against DateTime.now() on the device (supabase_repository.dart l.248); the 18+ age check is computed from the device clock (welcome_page.dart l.44-53, models.dart l.116-130); session_provider.dart writes updated_at from the device on the presence repair path (l.160, l.189); leaveCouple does the same (l.335). friendlyAuthError even tells users to check that their phone's date and time are automatic (auth_errors.dart l.13-15) — a support instruction standing in for a fix.

8. Foreground-and-online is assumed everywhere. There is no offline queue for identity operations. loadProfile is 5 serialized round trips gated on 10s timeouts; syncTimezone, registerToken and _refreshOnResume all fire on resume; the presence heartbeat is a 30s timer that exists only while the app is foregrounded (main.dart l.195-204). The inviter learns their partner joined by polling loadProfile, not by any push or subscription. Everything degrades to "kill the app and relaunch", which the code itself calls out (main.dart l.322-328).

9. Realtime is one websocket carrying feature-critical state with hand-rolled reconnect. Identity uses a Postgres-changes channel 'profile-sync:<coupleId>' filtered on profiles.couple_id — meaning every profile row change (including fcm_token writes on every resume, chat_theme_id, status_message) is broadcast to the partner. "Pattern A" (await removeChannel before re-subscribing) is copy-pasted across session_provider.dart l.212-235 and app_shell.dart l.85-100 because duplicate-topic channels froze the partner's state.

10. Client-side "self-healing" writes compensating for schema races. session_provider.dart l.146-165 and l.172-195 both read and repair presence.couple_id on every single app load, described in-comment as a ~200ms read "that prevents the entire app from breaking" — layered on top of a DB trigger (trg_sync_presence_couple_id) that already does the same thing. Two mechanisms, both running, neither trusted.

11. Mutable global statics coordinate the security UI. MilesApp.showRealApp, MilesApp.authInProgress, MilesApp.systemOverlayActive, MilesApp.setupCompletedOnce, AppLock.locked, stealthActive, passwordRecovery, SupabaseRepository.keyWasReplaced. Correctness depends on every call site setting and clearing them in a finally; a leak locks the user out or drops the disguise.

12. Dead and duplicated code paths still deployed. createCouple/create_couple RPC has zero callers; couples.active is written by leave_couple and read by nothing; couples.invite_code is nulled and nullable but still in the model (models.dart l.39) and still parsed on every couple load; FakeNewsScreen reimplements the CoverGate mixin used by the other three covers.

HIGHEST-CONFIDENCE DEFECTS FOR THE REDESIGN

A. session_provider.dart l.38-56 — SessionState.copyWith cannot write a null session (`session ?? this.session`). gotrue 2.22.0 emits signedOut with a null session on refresh-token rejection (gotrue_client.dart l.1496-1498), so a revoked/expired refresh token leaves isAuthenticated true forever. Every request 401s; the router never routes to /signin. Only a process restart recovers.

B. Both partners tapping "Create & get a code" permanently deadlocks pairing (create_pairing_invite creates and links a couple; redeem_pairing_invite then raises already_paired; CouplePage hides the join field once a code exists; _restoreInvite reproduces that state on every relaunch). Recovery requires Settings → Disconnect.

C. Cold-start deep links (email confirmation, password recovery, tethered://join) land behind the disguise cover with no hint that a hidden trigger exists.

D. redeem_pairing_invite's 2-member cap is an unlocked `select count(*)` (pairing_invites.sql l.81-82) with no unique constraint backing it — two concurrent redemptions can both pass.

E. profiles.fcm_token is one column, readable by the partner under profiles_select_self_or_partner, and rewritten on every app resume.

TRANSPORT SPRAWL — one message can travel four different ways and the module treats them as interchangeable: Realtime broadcast on a PUBLIC topic, postgres_changes with an RLS-evaluated filter, a REST catch-up query keyed on seq, and an FCM push fired by a per-row Postgres trigger. Nothing owns delivery; each path patches a hole in another, and each carries a slightly different Message (the broadcast one has seq=0 and no deletion flags until the DB echo reconciles it).

THE PUBLIC BROADCAST TOPIC IS THE SINGLE LARGEST DEFECT. `client.channel('mood_burst:$id')` appears with no `private: true` anywhere in E:/LDR/mobile/lib, and there is no realtime.messages authorization policy in any file under E:/LDR/supabase. The topic name is derived entirely from couple_id, which hardening_2026_08.sql itself (L25) documents as non-secret because it is the first path segment of every never-expiring public couple_media URL. That topic carries live text, image paths, typing, and a 'cleared' command, and the receiving handlers (_onMsgBroadcast, _onClearedBroadcast, _onMoodBurst) validate nothing — not sender membership, not couple, not anything. The Postgres side of this app has been carefully hardened (SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, column-level revokes, monotonic receipts, a couple_id guard trigger); the Realtime side has no authorization at all. Any redesign must start here.

SCHEMA DRIFT — reply_to_id, voice_path and video_path are written by the client and referenced by chat_media_cleanup.sql but are declared in NO migration. Storage buckets couple_media, couple_intimate and chat-bg likewise exist only in the dashboard (only capsule-media is created in SQL). E:/LDR/supabase/*.sql cannot rebuild this system. That blocks staging, DR, and any second environment.

RECEIPT MODEL IS SOUND, ITS PLUMBING IS NOT — receipts_v2.sql correctly deleted the clock from the problem (server-assigned seq, greatest() monotonicity, SECURITY DEFINER-only writes). But ack_delivered has exactly one call site, immediately followed by ack_read on the same value, and the FCM background handler acks nothing — so 'delivered' never renders for anyone, and 'seen' requires the partner to physically open the Chat tab. The best-engineered piece of the module is undermined by where it is called from.

LIFECYCLE ASSUMPTIONS THAT BREAK AT SCALE, explicitly: (a) app_shell.dart renders tabs in a Column, not an IndexedStack, so ChatScreen is disposed on every tab switch — channels torn down, 300 rows refetched, receipts frozen, broadcast fast path dead (ChatBroadcastService.active = null); (b) the broadcast fast path requires BOTH partners to have the chat mounted simultaneously; (c) the typing indicator requires the partner online AND foregrounded AND on the Chat tab; (d) both realtime paths are live-only and their entire recovery story is one REST query, so a socket gap plus a >500-message backlog silently truncates; (e) nothing about read state advances while the app is backgrounded, by design, because the FCM isolate only draws a notification.

WRITE AMPLIFICATION ON SHARED HOT PATHS — per open chat: one ack_read RPC + one presence UPSERT every 5 seconds forever, plus one presence UPSERT per received message, plus two presence writes per typing burst. presence and chat_receipts are both REPLICA IDENTITY FULL and in the realtime publication, so every one of those no-op writes also fans out a WAL event to the partner. Separately, every message INSERT synchronously triggers pg_net → an edge function that mints a fresh RSA-signed OAuth token and makes three outbound HTTPS calls, with no suppression for a recipient who is already connected.

RLS PERFORMANCE FOOTGUN — every couple-scoped policy calls public.current_user_couple_id() bare rather than `(select public.current_user_couple_id())`, so Postgres re-evaluates it per row instead of caching it as an InitPlan. This applies to messages, chat_receipts and profiles, and it is also what Realtime evaluates per change per subscriber.

NO PAGINATION ANYWHERE — fetch() is a hard limit of 300 newest rows, fetchSince() a hard 500. Older history is simply unreachable in the UI, _messages grows unbounded within a session, and every incoming message triggers a full re-sort of the whole list plus an O(n) linear scan per rendered bubble for reply previews.

QUALITY IS UNEVEN, NOT UNIFORMLY POOR — chat_selection.dart, chat_send_queue.dart and receipts_v2.sql are genuinely well-reasoned, with the failure modes documented in comments that match the code. Against that: text sends swallow their insert exception with no retry and no failure UI (silent permanent loss), video sends duplicate for the sender because the queue does not thread the id through, ChatInputBar's clear-conversation doc comment claims local-only behaviour while calling the irreversible both-sides hard delete, and _clearedBefore is a fully-wired render filter for a feature whose SharedPreferences key is never written. The comments in this codebase are unusually honest about past bugs, but several now describe intent rather than current behaviour — read the call sites, not the docstrings.

TRANSPORT SHAPE. Exactly one websocket per device (SupabaseService.client is a singleton), carrying 5 always-on channels plus 1-5 screen-scoped ones. Measured peak for one user: 10 concurrent topics (Chat tab + a pushed game screen, because go_router push keeps AppShell and its selected tab mounted underneath). A couple therefore holds ~16-20 topics. The scale ceiling is NOT connection count — it is (a) postgres_changes subscriptions × WAL volume × per-subscriber RLS evaluation, and (b) the FCM/edge-function fan-out, which is the fatal one.

TWO COMPETING RESUBSCRIBE PATTERNS. The codebase documents a correct 'Pattern A' (await removeChannel(old) BEFORE re-creating, because Supabase never dedupes by topic and unsubscribe() only schedules an async leave) and implements it properly in ManagedSubscription (realtime_service.dart:112-128) and in 5 hand-rolled copies. Two survivors still have the original bug: PartnerScreenNotifier._subscribe (partner_here_badge.dart:59, removeChannel NOT awaited) and TouchTraceCanvas._subscribe (touch_trace_canvas.dart:89, unsubscribe-then-immediately-recreate). AppShell also assigns _reachChannel in both _onReady (line 116) and _rearmAlwaysOn (line 97) with no guard, orphaning one. Any redesign should delete every hand-rolled copy and keep one primitive.

REALTIME AS A DOORBELL, NOT A PAYLOAD. Almost every postgres_changes callback in the app ignores payload.newRecord and issues a fresh REST SELECT instead (presence, care, reasons, capsules, cycle, desire, intimacy — all `callback: (_) => onChange()`). So every change costs a WAL record + a websocket frame + a PostgREST query per subscriber. This triples the cost of the exact thing that is already the bottleneck.

EPHEMERAL STATE PERSISTED TO A HOT ROW. public.presence is one row per user, ~25 columns, REPLICA IDENTITY FULL, written up to ~18 times a minute by six independent writers: a 30s foreground heartbeat, a 5s chat_last_read timer, typing start/stop, a 15s location tick, a write per navigation, and mood/avatar/photo changes. Typing and chat_last_read are sub-second facts that also have a working broadcast/receipt path — they do not need to be in Postgres at all.

ALL BROADCAST TOPICS ARE UNAUTHENTICATED. No channel anywhere passes RealtimeChannelConfig(private: true) — grep confirms zero occurrences. Supabase broadcast/presence authorization is off by default, so `call:<coupleId>` (SDP + ICE), `mood_burst:<coupleId>` (message text and images), `screen_presence:<coupleId>` (room-by-room movement), `touch:<coupleId>`, `touch_trace:`, `heartbeat:`, `capsule_proximity:` (raw lat/lon every 4s) are joinable by anyone holding the anon key and a couple UUID. hardening_2026_08.sql states plainly that couple UUIDs are not secret — they are the first path segment of every never-expiring couple_media URL. postgres_changes IS gated by RLS; broadcast is not. This is the largest security gap in the realtime layer and it gets worse, not better, with more users. Additionally mood_lamp_screen.dart:41 joins a literal global topic `mood_lamp:none` whenever couple is null.

COUPLE_ID IS THE ONLY SCOPING KEY. Every topic is `<feature>:<coupleId>`, every postgres_changes filter is couple_id=eq, and every RLS policy resolves through current_user_couple_id(). Both partners match their own filters, so each user receives and reacts to their OWN echoes as well as the partner's — doubling refetch traffic on presence.

ASSUMPTIONS THAT BREAK AT SCALE, BY KIND:
- Both users online simultaneously: every broadcast-only feature (touch map, touch trace, heartbeat, watch-together, together avatars, mood lamp, both games, in-game chat, capsule proximity). No persistence, no replay, no catch-up — a dropped socket loses the interaction permanently. Games work around this with a 900ms peer 'sync' request; nothing else does.
- App foregrounded: the 30s presence heartbeat, the 15s location loop, the 5s chat_last_read timer, and the FSI-permission cache all stop when Android freezes the process. Chat is the only feature with a real reconnect catch-up (_catchUp via fetchSince(maxSeq)) — every other postgres_changes screen silently misses whatever happened while the socket was down.
- Live websocket: everything except chat (FCM + catch-up), reach (FCM), calls (FCM + durable call_invites row), and care (FCM). All 15+ Closer/games/touch features are socket-only.
- Correct device clocks: mostly fixed. Writes are server-stamped (presence_server_time.sql trigger) and reads use ServerClock (NTP-style offset learned free from the heartbeat's RETURNING). Two holdouts still use raw DateTime.now(): Presence.lastSeenText (presence_service.dart:152) and ReachEvent.isActive (reach_repository.dart:29).
- Same network: only capsule proximity, and it is by design (local Haversine, coordinates never persisted).

DEAD AND UNREACHABLE CODE. TouchMapRepository.subscribe (`body_touches:<coupleId>`, touch_map_repository.dart:104) is defined and never called even though body_touches is in the publication. RealtimeService.coupleStream (realtime_service.dart:45) is never called. Three subscribed tables (care_nudges, love_reasons, cycle_events) have no CREATE TABLE and no publication statement anywhere in E:\LDR\supabase — the SQL directory is not a complete record of the deployed schema, which means the publication membership cannot be verified from this repo.

RECONNECT AMPLIFICATION. AppShell forces realtime.disconnect() + connect() on EVERY AppLifecycleState.resumed — including returns from the photo picker and camera, which the app's own comments note happen constantly. Each one triggers realtimeResumed, which synchronously fans out to every listener, each doing a leave + join. That is 10-20 phoenix frames per resume per user, all concentrated in the moment thousands of users unlock their phones."

ASSUMPTIONS THAT BREAK AT SCALE, by dependency:

BOTH USERS ONLINE + FOREGROUNDED: the realtime `call:<coupleId>` broadcast is the only live signalling path, and it exists only while `callControllerProvider` has been instantiated — which happens exclusively in `AppShell.build`. AppShell exists only while `MilesApp.showRealApp == true`, and main.dart:213-231 forces that false on every `paused`/`hidden`/`detached` and on every cold start. So "backgrounded" and "behind the disguise cover" are the same thing here, and both kill realtime signalling.

LIVE WEBSOCKET: re-subscription after a socket drop is owned by AppShell (`_rearmAlwaysOn` → `callController.reconnect()`), driven by `initRealtimeAutoResume()`'s onOpen hook. Nothing re-arms while the cover is up. AppShell also hard-cycles the socket (`realtime.disconnect()` then `connect()`) on every resume — at thousands of users that is a full reconnect storm per foreground event, on top of the presence heartbeat upsert every 30s (main.dart:194-203).

SAME NETWORK: when `_ensureRelay`'s 3-second budget misses (cold install, slow carrier, cold edge function), the call proceeds on STUN alone. The app's own banner states the consequence: calls then only work when both users are on the same wifi.

CORRECT DEVICE CLOCKS: all TURN cache validity is judged against `DateTime.now()` on the device — the 12h in-memory window, the 20h disk window, and the 60s failure backoff. A skewed clock either serves dead credentials or discards live ones. (Nothing else in calling reads a timestamp; `call_invites.created_at` is server-side `now()` and is never read.)

PUSH REACHABILITY WITHIN 30 SECONDS: `ttl: '30s'` on call pushes means FCM discards rather than queues. Combined with the caller's hardcoded 35s `_connectTimer`, the entire killed-app path has a fixed, unadjustable budget.

ONE DEVICE PER USER: `profiles.fcm_token` is a single scalar, and the signalling topic is per-COUPLE not per-DEVICE. There is no device registry, no session id, no call id on the wire (the broadcast envelope carries `from`/`kind`/`data` and nothing that identifies which call a signal belongs to).

SECURITY POSTURE, three findings that compound: (a) the `call:<coupleId>` broadcast is not a private channel and there is no `realtime.messages` RLS anywhere in E:/LDR/supabase — anyone with the anon key and a couple UUID can join, inject an offer, or send `hangup` to kill a live call; (b) `reach-notify` has no auth check and its triggers send no Authorization header, so it is publicly invocable and will ring any user whose ids you know; (c) TURN credentials are 24h, unscoped, minted per device with no server-side rate limit, and cached in plaintext SharedPreferences.

FIRE-AND-FORGET EVERYWHERE: `_insertInvite` is unawaited with an empty catch; `notify_call` uses `net.http_post` with no retry or dead-letter; `CallForegroundService.start/stop` swallow all errors; `reach-notify` always returns 200 even on FCM failure. There is no path by which a failed ring becomes visible to the caller, the callee, or an operator. The only diagnostics that exist (`CallStats`, `turnError`, the NO-RELAY banner) never leave the device.

NO LIFECYCLE RECONCILIATION: `call_invites.answered_at` is never written, no row is ever deleted or expired, no cron exists, the incoming-call notification is never cancelled, and `hangup` exists only as an ephemeral broadcast. The result is that a call's end state is recorded nowhere — which is why a stale invite plus an undismissable notification can resurrect a call that ended hours earlier.

DEAD WEIGHT: `call_invites` carries `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` and sits in the `supabase_realtime` publication, but no client subscribes to postgres_changes on it — every call pays full-row WAL and realtime fan-out of a multi-KB SDP for no consumer. The `_CallTaskHandler` foreground task is entirely empty. The `answered_at` column is unused.

MIGRATION HYGIENE: E:/LDR/supabase is a flat directory of hand-ordered `.sql` files with no migration runner, no `config.toml`, and no `app_secrets` migration at all (that table was created by hand). Two triggers hardcode the project ref `sopictusdonlvuezmfep` in their function bodies, so the schema is not reproducible in a second environment.

ONE GENUINE STRENGTH worth preserving in a redesign: media is true 1:1 peer-to-peer (or Cloudflare-relayed), so the backend carries zero media bytes and the per-call server cost is one row insert, one pg_net POST, one FCM send, and a periodic TURN credential mint. The scaling problems here are all in control-plane correctness, authorization, and lifecycle — not in media capacity.

**The E2EE story is one shared key, and it is the whole architecture's load-bearing wall.** One X25519 keypair per DEVICE (E:/LDR/mobile/lib/core/crypto_core.dart, secure-storage key `miles_x25519_priv_v1`), one ECDH+HKDF couple key held in a static, no ratchet, no versioning, no escrow. Consequences that repeat everywhere: (a) both partners hold the identical key, so "private from your partner" (Fantasy Jar) is a client-side filter, not cryptography; (b) `android:allowBackup="false"` (AndroidManifest.xml:54) means ANY reinstall or new phone by EITHER partner permanently destroys the couple's entire Closer history for BOTH of them, and only the rotating device knows it — the other is told "your partner may need to open Closer" (closer_load_result.dart:39-42), which is false; (c) `CryptoCore.clearCache()` has zero callers and sign-out (session_provider.dart:244) clears neither the derived key, the stored private key, nor the Memory-Threads PIN.

**Comments describe a system that isn't there.** `hmacTag` is documented as "HMAC-SHA256 with the couple-shared key" and is keyless 32-bit FNV-1a over a fixed 12-word taxonomy (crypto_core.dart:179-187) — so `fantasy_jar_entries.tag_hashes` is server-readable with a 12-entry lookup table. `afterglow_form_screen.dart:19-23` says "The sealed_at column is set here" and `startEntry` never sets it, while `fetchEntries` requires it NOT NULL, so Afterglow silently discards every entry users write; `completeAndSeal()` and `fetchPending()` have zero callers. Any redesign should treat inline comments in this repo as intent, not description.

**Four independent hand-rolled crypto packings.** `packMacAndCiphertext` = mac||ct (vault, memory threads, afterglow text), `fantasy_jar_repository._pack` and `body_map_repository._pack` = ct||mac (opposite order, duplicated verbatim in two files), `packFull` = nonce||mac||ct (afterglow photos). Plus three near-copies of the key-derivation preamble (closer_crypto.ensureSharedKey, fantasy_jar_repository.ensureSharedKey, body_map_repository.ensureSharedKey), only one of which the Closer entry screen calls.

**Privacy gates live in Dart, not in Postgres.** Desire's "reveal only if both >= 7" filters a response that already contains the partner's score. Fantasy Jar's "only the author sees it" is `.eq('author', myId)`. Pick-for-us tier consent is checked client-side. Capsule proximity unlock is checked client-side and `unlock_capsule()` (capsules.sql:91-95) simply doesn't validate mode='proximity'. Intimacy Signals is the only feature whose privacy rule is genuinely enforced in RLS — and its window is client-chosen, so a patched client can hold a permanent "active signal".

**Realtime broadcast is used as if it were authenticated. It isn't.** No channel anywhere in lib/ is created with `private: true`. Topics are `touch:<coupleId>`, `touch_trace:<coupleId>`, `mood_lamp:<coupleId>`, `capsule_proximity:<coupleId>`. hardening_2026_08.sql:24 states in its own words that couple UUIDs are not secret (first path segment of never-expiring couple_media URLs). So any authenticated stranger who learns a couple UUID can join and receive live GPS coordinates (proximity) and working 1-hour signed URLs to intimate photos (touch reactions).

**Nothing in Closer has a delivery path when the app is closed.** Grep across fcm_push.sql, message_push.sql, 20260628_care_call_push.sql, reach_events.sql and functions/reach-notify/index.ts finds zero references to any Closer table. Every Closer feature is either fetch-on-open or requires both partners simultaneously online and foregrounded on the same screen (touch trace, touch map, mood lamp, capsule proximity, breath). Six tables are published to `supabase_realtime` with `replica identity full` (closer_realtime.sql) that NO client subscribes to — paying WAL and replication cost for nothing.

**Dead schema, dead code.** Tables that exist, are RLS'd, and are never touched by the app: `consent_state`, `mood_lamp`, `fantasy_jar_reveals`, `couple_dissolutions`, `body_touches` (and with it `TouchMapRepository.sendTouch`/`subscribe`). `AfterglowRepository.completeAndSeal`/`fetchPending` are unreachable. Two unrelated features are both called "vault": `vault_items` (Closer, E2EE) and `personal_vault_items` (plaintext, PIN-gated) — private_vault.sql:5 even documents the collision.

**"Ephemeral" and "deleted" are labels, not behaviour.** `vault_items.reconfirm_due` (+90d), `vault_items.deleted=true`, `afterglow_entries.retention='ephemeral'`, `memory_threads.state='deleted'`, `body_touches.expires_at` (+10s) and expired `intimacy_signals` are all written and never acted on. The only `cron.schedule` calls in E:/LDR/supabase are in breath_events.sql and reach_pulses.sql. Nothing purges Closer, and `couple_intimate/<coupleId>/reactions/*` grows forever with no cleanup path.

**Large media goes into Postgres, not object storage.** Vault photos, Memory-Threads photos and Afterglow photos are picked at `imageQuality: 85` with no `maxWidth`/`maxHeight`, encrypted whole, hex-encoded (≈2x on the wire) and inserted into `bytea` columns. Every list screen then does a bare `.select()` — all columns, all rows, no pagination — so opening the vault or the memory timeline downloads every photo the couple has ever saved. This is the single biggest cost and latency cliff at scale.

**Device clocks are load-bearing.** Vault's 14-day mutual-consent delete window (`private_vault_repository.dart:118-121`), Desire's `on_date` day key (both submit and read), Intimacy Signals' `window_expires_at` and `isActive`, Capsule's `dateConditionMet`, Mood Lamp's 4-hour fade. `E:/LDR/mobile/lib/core/services/server_clock.dart` exists and is used by presence — no Closer feature uses it.

**An unreported account-deletion bug.** `delete_my_account()` (E:/LDR/supabase/account_deletion.sql) deletes `auth.users`, cascading to `profiles`. But `vault_items.created_by`, `vault_items.delete_requested_by`, `vault_items.deleted_by` and `memory_threads.accepted_by` reference `public.profiles(id)` with NO `ON DELETE CASCADE` (E:/LDR/supabase/intimacy_tables.sql:79, 84, 87, 137). When a user with vault items deletes their account while the partner is still in the couple (so the couple row and its cascade are not triggered), the profile delete violates those foreign keys and the RPC raises — the Play-required in-app deletion path fails for exactly the users who have used Closer. Unverified by execution; this is a static read of the constraint definitions, and there is no migration elsewhere in E:/LDR/supabase that adds the cascade.

**Unversioned infrastructure.** The `couple_intimate` bucket — which holds body photos and touch reactions — is never created and has no storage policies in ANY file under E:/LDR/supabase; it is referenced by account_deletion.sql, chat_media_cleanup.sql and touch_photo_delete.sql but its RLS exists only in the Supabase dashboard. `capsule-media` is the only intimate-adjacent bucket whose policies are in source control (capsules.sql:110-121), and its SELECT policy ignores `unlocked_at`, so sealed capsule media is listable and signable before the capsule opens.

PATTERNS THAT REPEAT ACROSS MODULES

1) "Both online, same screen, right now" is the default delivery model. Truth or Dare, Never Have I Ever / Would You Rather, the in-game chat strip, Together, Watch Together, Heartbeat, Breath Sync and capsule proximity all carry their entire state in each client's setState and synchronise over ephemeral Supabase Realtime BROADCAST. Nothing is stored, nothing is replayed, and there is no "you missed this". If one partner arrives ten seconds late, or their socket dropped during Android doze, the interaction never happened — and the UI never says so. For a long-distance app spanning timezones this is the single most structurally wrong assumption in the product.

2) Every broadcast channel is public and named `<feature>:<coupleId>`. There is no RealtimeChannelConfig(private: true) anywhere in the client and no RLS policy on realtime.messages in any .sql file. Any authenticated user who knows a couple_id can join game_td:, gchat:, gcard:, heartbeat:, together:, watch:, screen_presence: and the capsule proximity channel — reading plaintext chat, heart rate and coarse GPS, and injecting cards or messages. hardening_2026_08.sql:25 itself notes that couple_id is not secret because it is the first path segment of every public couple_media URL.

3) Device clocks are load-bearing in at least four places, even though ServerClock (core/services/server_clock.dart) exists and is used only by Presence. Breath Sync compares a partner's device epoch-ms against local now (a >19s skew means it never syncs). Reach discards any event whose server-set expires_at is behind the local clock, so a fast clock silently swallows every alert. Cycle events are stamped with the device's calendar date. Daily Prompt keys its row on the device's calendar date, which is why two partners in different timezones create and answer two different prompts and the reveal never fires.

4) Foreground-only by construction. Location sharing runs only while the Home TAB is open (not merely while the app is open). The presence heartbeat, the 15s presence poll, ChatSendQueue's in-memory upload queue, and every broadcast feature stop dead when Android freezes the process. The only true background path is FCM, and it delivers content-free notifications by design.

5) Push is one function doing an OAuth handshake per message. reach, care, call and message all trigger pg_net → the same reach-notify edge function → a freshly minted service-account JWT → Google token exchange → FCM. No token cache, no batching, one fcm_token column per user (multi-device is impossible), 200-on-every-error so failures are invisible, and pg_net discards responses.

6) Durable Postgres used as an event bus. breath_events writes a row per 19-second breathing cycle; reach_events, care_nudges and love_reasons all trigger full-list refetches (unbounded SELECTs, no pagination) on every realtime event; every navigation writes presence. Meanwhile reach_pulses, visit_memories, mood_lamp, consent_state, couple_dissolutions and fantasy_jar_reveals are schema'd, RLS'd and never used.

7) The backend is not the schema of record. Four client-used tables (care_nudges, cycle_settings, cycle_events, love_reasons) and three storage buckets (couple_media, couple_intimate, chat-bg) have no DDL in E:/LDR/supabase. There are no migrations/, no config.toml, no applied-order lockfile — 43 loose files where later ones patch earlier ones. Nothing can be rebuilt, staged, reviewed or rolled back.

8) Features wired to promises they do not keep. Rituals persists a delivery time and nothing ever delivers (and prints the same local time twice, labelling one "their time"). Ads is hardcoded off with placeholder unit IDs while still pulling the AD_ID permission. Pooled love notes are flag-disabled but ship 250 hardcoded paragraphs in every APK. The Vault says "zero bytes touch device storage" but stores a revocable pointer to a public URL and opens it in the SYSTEM BROWSER. Modest mode claims both partners must consent and is a single boolean either can flip. Proximity capsules are unlockable from anywhere because unlock_capsule only validates dates. Care nudges push a blank generic notification, so the reminder never reaches a backgrounded partner.

9) Inconsistent privacy posture for media. Chat photos, avatars and Home check-ins go to the PUBLIC couple_media bucket with never-expiring getPublicUrl links; videos and body photos go to the private couple_intimate bucket with signed URLs. Same app, same threat model, two answers.

10) Three fixes exist but were not applied everywhere. ManagedSubscription (the awaited-removeChannel pattern) is the canonical primitive, but cycle_screen.dart:64-75 and its Home card still use unsubscribe()+re-channel() with the same topic. NetImage decodes at display size, but MediaViewer uses raw Image.network. ServerClock corrects presence freshness but nothing else.

11) Free third-party infrastructure with no contract on hot paths: CARTO basemap tiles on the HOME screen, maplibre-gl fetched from unpkg into an unrestricted WebView plus ArcGIS/AWS/openfreemap tiles for the 3D map, and BBC/NPR/Al Jazeera RSS fetched directly from every device (with a spoofed User-Agent) to render the disguise cover. Each of these throttles or blocks at volume, and the RSS one fails the disguise precisely when it matters.

12) One genuinely good pattern worth preserving in the redesign: the split between `updated_at` (any write, including GPS) and `app_last_active_at` (genuine app activity only, stamped by a server-side BEFORE trigger), read through ServerClock with a 45s freshness window. It is the only place in the app where "is my partner here" is computed honestly, and it is the model the other eleven presence-shaped features should have been built on.

scale_risks.why: Every token refresh and every foreground resume costs 5 serialized DB round trips per user plus a presence write; at thousands of users that is a constant multiplied read load with no caching, and the null-session bug produces permanently wedged clients that keep retrying.

The funnel converts any transient backend failure into a user-visible dead end, and the number of distinct stuck states grows with the number of onboarding stages. It is the single highest-support-cost surface in the app.

Both-create deadlock and the clock-dependent expiry check are user-visible failures that need manual recovery; the unlocked member-count check is a genuine race that only appears under concurrency; and the inviter's 'did they join yet' answer is delivered by polling a 5-query loadProfile.
Unbounded orphaned data (couples, messages, storage objects) with no reaper, plus a silent state change for the other party that the router turns into an unexplained onboarding bounce.

Single-token-per-user is a schema-level ceiling that breaks multi-device outright, the partner-readable token is a privacy leak that RLS currently permits, and the per-resume write multiplies with user count.

postgres_changes re-evaluates the messages RLS policy per change per connected subscriber, and the policy calls public.current_user_couple_id() unwrapped (not `(select ...)`), so it is re-evaluated per row rather than cached as an InitPlan. Every open chat holds 3 channels. The public broadcast topic is a confidentiality and integrity hole that scales linearly with user count — one leaked couple_id is a full live wiretap. The 300-row no-pagination fetch on every tab switch multiplies REST load by navigation frequency.

On flaky mobile networks at population scale this is a steady background rate of vanished messages with zero telemetry and zero user-visible signal — the classic 'she never texted me' failure the repo's own message_push.sql comment describes, reintroduced on the write side.

scale_risks.module: chat.send.media (image / video / voice / GIF) + optimistic send queue
scale_risks.why: Unversioned, undocumented storage buckets cannot be recreated in a new environment. Public bucket + couple_id-in-path is a systemic privacy exposure, not a per-user one. Per-message uploads are direct client→Storage with no CDN caching strategy, size cap enforcement server-side, or media lifecycle/TTL; storage grows without bound because nothing prunes messages.

Two writes every 5 seconds per open chat (one RPC + one presence UPSERT), forever, regardless of whether anything changed. 1,000 concurrent open chats = ~400 writes/sec of pure no-op churn against chat_receipts and presence, both of which are in the realtime publication with REPLICA IDENTITY FULL, so each write also fans out a WAL change to the partner's subscriber.

Three outbound HTTPS calls plus a fresh RSA-signed OAuth exchange per message inserted, synchronously coupled to the write path via a per-row trigger. A single busy couple in a rapid exchange generates dozens of edge invocations per minute; at thousands of users this saturates pg_net's queue and the edge function's concurrency long before Postgres itself is stressed, and the failure mode is silent.

Per user this is 1 socket, which is fine; the problem is the reconnect storm. Every app resume = 1 socket close + 1 open + N phx_leave + N phx_join, where N is 5-10. At thousands of users with typical mobile foreground/background churn, that is a sustained join-rate load on the Realtime tenant, not a steady-state connection count problem. Supabase enforces a channel-joins-per-second ceiling; this design maximises joins per user-minute.

1 websocket/user is cheap. 5-10 channels/user is not: each postgres_changes channel is an independent subscription that Supabase Realtime must evaluate — with RLS — against every WAL change on that table. With 8 postgres_changes tables and thousands of users, the Realtime tenant does O(subscribers) RLS evaluations per row change. This is the classic postgres_changes ceiling and it is reached long before the raw connection count matters.

presence is the single hottest table in the system: ~18 writes/user/minute of a wide row with REPLICA IDENTITY FULL, all replicated. At 2,000 concurrent users that is ~36,000 writes/min and 36,000 full-row WAL messages/min feeding Realtime, before any fan-out multiplier. Nothing is batched, coalesced, or moved off Postgres.

Per user: 4 unconditional SELECTs/min from the poll, plus up to ~1.25 SELECTs/s during a chat session (partner writes chat_last_read every 5s, and the local user's own writes echo back too). Realtime is being used as an expensive doorbell for a query. At thousands of users this is a PostgREST/PgBouncer load problem as much as a Realtime one.
Ephemeral, sub-second state is being persisted to a replicated row. This is the single clearest write-amplification in the app and it scales with keystroke bursts, not with users.

Two round-trips plus a geocode every 15 seconds per user with Home open. Location is also the reason presence rows are wide, which is why every unrelated presence write is an expensive WAL record. This will not survive thousands of users on the same table.

Three concurrent subscriptions per chatting user, one of which (messages) is a postgres_changes subscription on the app's highest-volume table, plus a 12/min presence write. Two people chatting is ~6 realtime subscriptions, ~24 presence writes/min, ~24 partner SELECTs/min, and one FCM push per message regardless of whether the recipient is already looking at the screen.

scale_risks.module: FCM push layer (tokens, triggers, edge function, background isolate)
scale_risks.why: This is the hard ceiling. Every chat message triggers one synchronous pg_net enqueue plus one edge-function invocation that performs an RSA signature and a Google OAuth exchange before sending — per message, per couple, with no token cache, no batching, and no suppression for online recipients. At thousands of users chatting this is edge-function invocations and Google token-endpoint calls scaling linearly with total message volume, and pg_net's single fire-and-forget queue plus an unbounded net._http_response table sits directly in the write path of the busiest table in the app.

REPLICA IDENTITY FULL across ~28 tables plus a subquery-based RLS predicate is the exact combination that makes Supabase postgres_changes fall over: the replication payload is maximal and the authorisation check is a query, evaluated per subscriber per row change. The repo also cannot be trusted as the source of truth for what is actually in the publication, which is itself a scale/ops risk.

The topic is an unauthenticated, guessable-by-UUID public broadcast room; call teardown and call injection are available to anyone who can enumerate or obtain a couple id. Beyond security, the design needs both apps foregrounded and unlocked-past-the-cover with a live websocket to work at all — the realtime path is best-effort at every hop, and the couple-scoped topic means no multi-device story exists.

scale_risks.module: Durable offer store (`call_invites`) and the ring trigger
scale_risks.why: Unbounded growth of SDP blobs with full-row replication and a realtime publication nobody reads is pure cost per call. More seriously, the ring is a fire-and-forget pg_net POST with no retry and no observability, and a never-expired invite row makes stale calls answerable indefinitely.

scale_risks.module: Push ring delivery (`reach-notify` edge function → FCM)
scale_risks.why: An unauthenticated, internet-reachable endpoint that rings arbitrary users' phones is an abuse vector on day one of public scale, and it does two Google auth round trips per push. The single `fcm_token` column caps every user at one device.

Cloudflare TURN is billed on relayed bandwidth and there is no server-side quota, per-user cap, or per-call credential scoping — one leaked 24h credential is a metered relay for anyone. The fallback when acquisition misses its 3s budget is a same-network-only call, which is the dominant failure mode once users are on real carrier NATs.

scale_risks.module: Incoming-call notification, full-screen intent, and the disguise cover gate
scale_risks.why: This is the only path that works when the callee is not already inside the unlocked app, and it is missing the two things a ring needs: cancellation and inline accept/decline. At scale the visible symptom is stale, undismissable 'incoming call' notifications accumulating on devices, plus a ring the user cannot answer without passing biometrics inside the caller's 35-second window.

The primary real-world calling scenario — partner's phone in a pocket, app not running — depends on a 30-second-TTL push, a hand-mirrored FSI permission flag, a biometric unlock, and a full app cold start all completing inside a hardcoded 35-second caller timeout, with no cancellation, no retry, and no state reconciliation when any link fails.

scale_risks.module: Key exchange + CryptoCore (the crypto under all of Closer)
scale_risks.why: Phone replacement is a routine event; here it silently destroys the couple's entire encrypted history for both people with no recovery and a misleading error message. At thousands of users this is a continuous, unfixable support queue plus real data loss. Also blocks any server-side feature (search, moderation, retention enforcement, migration) forever.

Unbounded bytea photo storage in Postgres with no purge job, no pagination, and a full-table fetch on screen open. Storage cost and query latency grow linearly with couple lifetime and blow up Postgres/PostgREST rather than object storage.

The product's core privacy promise (soft matches, never the raw text) is enforced only client-side and the tag anonymisation is reversible with a 12-entry lookup table. That is a headline-grade disclosure across the whole user base, not a per-couple bug.

Same unbounded-blob-in-Postgres pattern as the vault plus a full-table fetch, and a gate whose PIN storage would not survive scrutiny. Deleted memories are retained indefinitely, which is a data-subject-deletion problem once users are strangers.

Ships as a dead feature that silently discards user-authored intimate content — worse than absent. Everything else about it (blobs in Postgres, unenforced ephemerality) is the same scaling failure as the vault.

A server-side authorization gap (proximity unlock), a seal bypass through storage, and live GPS on an unauthenticated-by-topic broadcast channel. All three are exploitable by any registered stranger who learns a couple UUID.

scale_risks.module: Touch Map (the shipped one — broadcast only)
scale_risks.why: Intimate-media signed URLs broadcast on a topic keyed by a non-secret UUID, on a bucket whose policies are not in source control, with unbounded storage growth and no retention. This is the highest-consequence disclosure surface in the suite.

Per active user with Home open: 4 presence SELECTs + 4 presence UPSERTs + 4 geocodes per minute for location, plus 4 presence SELECTs/min from the provider poll, plus 2 heartbeat upserts/min. That is ~14 DB ops/user/minute at idle before anyone touches anything; 1,000 concurrent users ≈ 14k writes+reads/min against one Postgres row set with replica identity full and realtime fan-out on every write.

Free tile CDNs will throttle or block the app's User-Agent long before thousands of users; the map is on the HOME screen, so every session hits it. Requires migrating to a paid tile provider (or self-hosting) before launch.

Backend object is not reproducible from source (no DDL, no RLS in repo), full 50-row refetch on every event, and an unbounded per-message pg_net → edge function → FCM chain with no batching or throttle.

Unfiltered postgres_changes subscriptions on a table with thousands of users mean Realtime evaluates RLS per subscriber per change; two such subscriptions are mounted (Home card + screen). Combined with no DDL/no index guarantees and no server-side prediction, this is the module least ready for multi-tenant load.

~3 INSERTs/user/minute plus a Realtime fan-out and a full trigger/WAL cycle per tick, for data with a 19-second useful life, retained a full day. A broadcast channel would cost zero writes. 1,000 concurrent breathers = 3,000 durable writes/min.

Every reach is a Postgres INSERT + trigger + pg_net HTTP call + edge function cold start + Google OAuth token exchange (the token is minted per invocation, never cached, functions/reach-notify/index.ts:51-90) + FCM send. That is a full OAuth round trip per notification for every reach, care nudge, call and CHAT MESSAGE in the system — the single hardest bottleneck in the push path.

~70-90 broadcast messages per user per minute — by far the highest realtime message rate in the app. 100 concurrent pairs ≈ 15,000 Realtime messages/minute for a feature with zero durable value, and Supabase bills broadcast messages.

scale_risks.module: App shell, navigation and screen-presence publishing
scale_risks.why: A per-navigation write amplification pattern plus a per-foreground socket storm. Thousands of users backgrounding/foregrounding produce synchronized reconnect + rejoin bursts against Supabase Realtime, which is exactly the load pattern that causes channel-join throttling.

Every single user-visible event in the app (every chat message, reach, nudge, call) becomes: trigger → pg_net HTTP → edge function cold start → OAuth token exchange → profiles lookup ×2 → FCM POST. At thousands of users this saturates pg_net's worker queue and Google's token endpoint quota; it needs batching, a cached token, and a proper worker/queue rather than per-row HTTP from Postgres.
No reproducible environment means no staging, no reviewable RLS change, no rollback and no disaster recovery. Every other scaling fix in this list is gated on fixing this first.
